rows.basis: untested proposal; the staging follows [fading support](claims/fading-support-promotes-transfer-of-responsibility.md) [~S], which was tested on worked examples, not supervision
rows.change: Judge readiness on observed unaided performance on representative tasks, not on how well the learner discusses them with the expert; withdraw the expert's presence in stages (present, then on call, then reviewing afterwards)
rows.if: Stakes are high (licensure, patient or client safety)

rows.basis: untested proposal; one small comparison found fewer mentored than unmentored new teachers reached the most developed concern level and raised whether mentors held mentees back ([Teachers without mentors reached the impact level more often than mentored teachers, raising the question that mentoring may inhibit development](claims/mentors-may-inhibit-concern-development.md) [~W], associational, 39 teachers)
rows.change: Plan from the start when the mentor will ask more and tell less, and check at the midpoint whether the mentee is proposing their own solutions
rows.if: A long mentoring relationship (a year, a probation period)

rows.basis: [Minimal guidance is less effective for novices than explicit instruction](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S]
rows.change: Open with one worked example or short explanation; then a single, narrow "why" prompt per step; give a model answer after each attempt; no open discovery task first.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` for this relation

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Drop the opening example and step-by-step prompts; give an unfamiliar case to explain, or two solutions to compare and choose between, and ask for a justification.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` for this relation

rows.basis: [Self-explanation prompts improve learning from worked examples](claims/self-explanation-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+M] (pooled across levels of education, and one study with eighth graders; the adaptations themselves are untested)
rows.change: Keep the "why" prompts but allow spoken answers; use two concrete cases rather than abstract descriptions; one relation per session.
rows.if: Learners are children or young adolescents (`child`, `adolescent`)

rows.basis: [Comparing contrasting cases improves learning](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M] (the transfer experiment was with undergraduates learning negotiation; untested in workplace training)
rows.change: Draw the two cases for comparison from the learners' own work, differing on the one feature that matters, and ask what they share before naming the principle.
rows.if: Learners are adults or professionals (`adult`, `adult-workplace`)

rows.basis: [Comparing contrasting cases improves learning](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [~M] (one algebra study: procedural and flexibility gains, no added conceptual gain)
rows.change: Compare two solution methods side by side and ask when each is better; expect gains in using and choosing methods, and check conceptual understanding separately.
rows.if: The goal is a `procedure`

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do not build explanation or comparison tasks around isolated facts; use retrieval with feedback, and keep activation for the relations among the facts.
rows.if: The goal is facts or vocabulary (`verbal-association`)

rows.basis: [Self-explanation prompts improve learning from worked examples](claims/self-explanation-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+M] (prompting is tested; the reveal-after-commit step is untested)
rows.change: Put the prompt in the material with a required typed answer before the model explanation is revealed; the learner then compares the two.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: [Teachers had minimal success designing Constructive and Interactive activities](claims/teachers-struggle-designing-interactive-activities.md) [~M] and [Students learned more in Constructive than Active activities](claims/students-learned-more-constructive-than-active.md) [+M]
rows.change: Before teaching, check each planned task against step 4 (does the output go beyond the material?), with a colleague if possible; expect tasks planned as interactive to come out merely active.
rows.if: `classroom` with a teacher designing their own tasks

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: One relation, one activating task, one probe at the end; leave comparison of methods and justification for later. In a unit (`days-weeks`), sequence example, then prompts, then comparison, then justification, with a delayed probe.
rows.if: One session only (`single-session`)

rows.basis: [Self-explanation prompts improve learning from worked examples](claims/self-explanation-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [~M] (evidence for classroom and delayed gains much more limited)
rows.change: Add at least one changed-case item to the assessment, and a delayed one if retention matters; do not read an immediate gain as durable.
rows.if: Stakes: the assessment is recall-only or the gain must last

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Accept explanations in the first language, orally, or with a sentence frame, so the task tests the relation rather than the wording.
rows.if: Learners work in a second language of instruction

rows.basis: [Part-task practice reduces cognitive load for absolute novices during initial skill acquisition.](claims/part-task-practice-reduces-load-for-novices.md) [~M]; population not reported on the claim page
rows.change: Start with one case and part tasks; add the second and third case only after the simple version is completed unaided; prompt the named dimension of comparison.
rows.if: Expertise `novice` in the domain, high element interactivity

rows.basis: [Presenting multiple cases from different perspectives supports transfer in ill-structured domains](claims/cognitive-flexibility-theory-multiple-cases.md) [+M]; tested with first- and second-year undergraduates, untested with professionals
rows.change: Use criss-crossing: revisit each concept in several short cases under different themes across sessions; drop the step-by-step part tasks.
rows.if: Expertise `intermediate` or `advanced`, an ill-structured domain (clinical reasoning, law, policy)

rows.basis: untested proposal; no claim here tests this relationship with children
rows.change: Use two cases at a time, side by side, with the one dimension that differs named by the teacher; no free navigation among cases.
rows.if: Age `child` (under 12)

rows.basis: [Comparing cases side by side improves learning and transfer by a moderate average amount, though in one algebra study it raised procedural knowledge and flexibility but not conceptual knowledge](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [~M]; tested with seventh-graders, procedural flexibility rose, conceptual knowledge did not
rows.change: Have learners compare alternative solution methods side by side; expect gains in choosing methods, and add a separate item asking why each method works.
rows.if: Age `adolescent`, goal a mathematics `procedure`

rows.basis: [Presenting multiple cases from different perspectives supports transfer in ill-structured domains](claims/cognitive-flexibility-theory-multiple-cases.md) [~M]: the drill group recalled more facts
rows.change: Do not make criss-crossing the main activity; give facts their own retrieval practice, and use varied cases only for the transfer part of the objective.
rows.if: Goal `verbal-association` (facts, terms), or recall-weighted high-stakes assessment

rows.basis: [Multiple representations improve learning](claims/multiple-representations-improve-learning.md) [~M]; one undergraduate physics field study and a review; benefit depends on representational competence
rows.change: Add a second representation (sketch, simulation) beside the formula, with tasks that connect them; monitor reported load and representational skill.
rows.if: Goal a STEM `concept` taught through representations

rows.basis: [Students in the flexible hypertext-based course design scored higher on achievement tests (76%) than students in the direct online course design (59%)](claims/cft-hypertext-design-higher-achievement-scores.md) [~W]: groups studied different software, so it does not isolate the design; navigation burden is untested, from the theory page
rows.change: Give a guided route through the cases (a theme per pass) rather than free browsing, and build the comparison prompts into the pages.
rows.if: Setting `online-self-paced` or hypertext

rows.basis: [Comparing cases side by side improves learning and transfer by a moderate average amount, though in one algebra study it raised procedural knowledge and flexibility but not conceptual knowledge](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M]: comparison helped in single experiments, more at immediate tests
rows.change: Use two or three contrasting cases with a similarities prompt and the principle stated after; test on a new case the same day. If the course allows, revisit the cases later under a new theme.
rows.if: Duration `single-session`

rows.basis: [Presenting multiple cases from different perspectives supports transfer in ill-structured domains](claims/cognitive-flexibility-theory-multiple-cases.md) [+M]: the advantage appeared by the fourth session; delayed benefit untested
rows.change: Return to the same concepts in each session through new cases and new themes; schedule a delayed transfer case.
rows.if: Duration `days-weeks` or `term-plus`

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep cases short, give them in accessible language, and present the comparison as a table learners fill in, so reading demand does not swamp comparison.
rows.if: Constraint: cases in a second language, or heavy reading load

rows.basis: [Items should represent essential skills in a teaching hierarchy](claims/criterion-referenced-items-should-represent-essential-skills-in-a-teaching-hierarchy.md) [+W] (an argument about reading tests, carried to other domains)
rows.change: Use short criterion-referenced checks on the first skills in the teaching order, three to five items per skill; report mastered / not yet per skill; no percentiles
rows.if: The decision is what to teach next for `novice` learners early in a domain

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Add items at the upper skills of the hierarchy, or a broader task, so the check is not at ceiling; if relative standing matters (an enrichment place), use a norm-referenced score from an above-level test and a work sample
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or near the top of the range

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do not use one sitting for a placement; use an individually administered criterion-referenced check with pictures and spoken instructions over two or three occasions; re-check within the year
rows.if: Learners are young children (`child`) in screening or readiness testing

rows.basis: [SAT underpredicts girls' performance](claims/sat-underpredicts-girls-performance.md) [~W]; [MIT lower SAT math, equal performance](claims/mit-lower-sat-math-scores-equal-performance.md) [~W] (1987 testimony, no data printed)
rows.change: Use the norm-referenced score with at least one other piece of evidence; look again at everyone near the cut; check the norm group fits the applicants
rows.if: The decision is selection for limited places (a programme, a scholarship, admission)

rows.basis: [Identification tests cannot fully determine learning potential](claims/traditional-identification-tests-fail-learning-potential.md) [~W] (a review section); [diverse students under-identified nationwide](claims/gifted-underrepresentation-diverse-students.md) [~W] (an issue brief); the dual-measure requirement is the earlier page's
rows.change: Build a diagnostic profile: a norm-referenced aptitude or ability measure plus achievement, classroom observation and a classroom-learning task; screen all learners rather than relying on referral; compare identification rates by group with enrolment
rows.if: The decision is gifted or special-education identification

rows.basis: [Statistical item selection undermines criterion-referenced definitions](claims/statistical-item-selection-conflicts-criterion-referenced-definition.md) [+W]; [criterion-referenced tests need construct validation](claims/criterion-referenced-tests-need-construct-validation.md) [+W] (both Nitko 1970, arguments)
rows.change: Define skills before items; keep items that nearly everyone passes after teaching; set the cut by a stated panel or rule before scoring; check a sample of classifications against real tasks once a term
rows.if: You are writing your own criterion-referenced test

rows.basis: [DC lowest at the distribution peak](claims/dc-lowest-at-score-distribution-peak.md) [~M] (simulated data, a measurement property, not a test of the remedy)
rows.change: Expect the least consistent decisions there: give near-cut learners a second, parallel check before deciding, or report "borderline" as its own category
rows.if: Most learners score close to the cut (a pass/fail examination where the cut sits at the most common score)

rows.basis: [Mean-classification method more robust to outliers](claims/mean-classification-cut-score-method-robust.md) [~M]; [agreement 71% to 97%](claims/body-of-work-agreement-rates-71-97.md) [~M] (one state's alternate portfolio assessment for students with significant disabilities, carried to other assessments)
rows.change: Use independent classification of real work samples, compute the cut from each sample's mean classification, and report panelist agreement with the cut
rows.if: A panel will set the cut (a programme standard, a licensing threshold)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do not read a low percentile as low subject knowledge; check the norm group included learners with this language background; add a low-language criterion-referenced check (spoken, pictorial, or practical) on the same skills
rows.if: Learners take the test in a second language, or have low literacy

rows.basis: untested; the reason not to rank is Gentile's argument ([competitive grading pits students against each other](claims/competitive-grading-pits-students-against-each-other.md) [-W])
rows.change: Report criterion-referenced results privately and per skill ("not yet" with the next step), never as a rank; keep norm-referenced results out of routine feedback
rows.if: Learners have low confidence or are anxious about tests

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: The learner (or family, for a child) decides who sees the full profile; share with teachers only the skills to teach and the supports agreed; never post or rank
rows.if: Results are private or sensitive (a diagnostic profile, a disability assessment)

rows.basis: untested proposal; the threshold model is [Competency-Based Assessment](principles/competency-based-assessment.md)'s
rows.change: Use a criterion-referenced judgment on tasks sampled from the job, with the cut set before scoring; use a norm-referenced score only if places are limited, and then with a work sample
rows.if: Adults in work settings: licensing, certification or job entry

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Judge the whole performance against criteria the audience would recognize; do not split it into paper items to get skill scores; record per-criterion notes from the one performance instead
rows.if: The brief wants a whole-task performance kept whole (a recital, a clinical scenario, a product for a real audience)

rows.basis: untested; the three changes follow steps 4, 5 and 9
rows.change: Keep them as the criteria; change only what the evidence here says matters: set the levels before scoring, report per criterion rather than as a rank, and take a second look at learners on a level boundary
rows.if: The brief names its own rubric, categories or reporting levels

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Check two or three skills with three items each rather than every skill thinly; rotate skills across checks
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (one 15-minute slot per check)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use a criterion-referenced placement check on the entry skills, 20 to 30 minutes; treat near-cut results as provisional and re-check in the first week of teaching
rows.if: Only a single session is available (a one-off placement)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give the same items, time and aids in every mode, or record the difference beside each result; keep items short and single-screen for phones; compare results by mode before pooling
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners in the room, some remote, some on phones only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Learners self-score short checks against an answer key with worked reasons; the teacher spends contact time only on near-cut learners and the skill most learners have not mastered
rows.if: One teacher for many learners, or facilitator time is scarce (volunteers, a short weekly session)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Report the percentage reaching each level with the number tested, and the level definitions; do not compare schools on a norm-referenced percentile alone; see [High-Stakes Testing and Accountability Effects](principles/high-stakes-testing-accountability-effects.md)
rows.if: Results are reported for accountability (school, district or programme reports)

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: List the candidate explanations and gather one observation that separates them (a task in the test's format, a look at what the test covers) before changing either
rows.if: A parent or learner asks why a classroom grade and a test score disagree

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Teach the difference with short worked examples and a tap-to-sort activity (statements sorted into "tells you what I can do" and "tells you how I rank"), and assess with auto-scored items against a stated criterion; do not ask learners to write test items on a phone
rows.if: Self-paced mobile study for school-age learners with no live teacher

rows.basis: [Advance organizers aided learning in a 1980 meta-analysis, but activating prior topic knowledge did not improve primary pupils' text comprehension in one experiment](claims/activation-improves-learning.md) [~M] (carried from topic-knowledge activation in reading to cultural connection)
rows.change: Teach the concept explicitly first, with one familiar context as the example; ask for learners' own contexts only after they can explain the concept once
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the content and have little experience related to it

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page's target learners
rows.change: Make cases from learners' work and lives the main material from the second session; ask each learner for one case per unit, and compare across them
rows.if: Learners are `adult`, in work or with family responsibilities

rows.basis: [Assessment tasks built on family-identified funds of knowledge elicited computational thinking from K-2 children in a small design-based study that made no comparison with standard assessment](claims/funds-of-knowledge-tasks-reveal-computational-thinking.md) [+M] (13 children, two tasks, no comparison with a standard task; resource-intensive)
rows.change: Build assessment tasks from practices families describe in interviews, as play with cards and objects, and ask children to justify their choices
rows.if: Learners are young children (`child`, K-2)

rows.basis: [Positioning personal experience as an epistemic resource supports expansion from inward to outward critical orientations](claims/positioning-personal-experience-as-epistemic-resource-supports-critical-orientation-expansion.md) [+W] (69 students, 12th-grade English, one site)
rows.change: Start from learners' own experience of the topic, then add readings and structured discussion that move it to systemic causes over several weeks; collect writing at the start and end
rows.if: Goal is critical analysis or civic understanding (`attitude-motivation`, `principle`)

rows.basis: [Learners invest more effort in tasks they perceive as interesting, personally important, or useful to their future goals.](claims/task-value-increases-motivation-and-engagement.md) [+M] (reviews of utility-value writing; the trade-off with practice is untested)
rows.change: Keep connections to one opening example and a short weekly utility-value reflection; do not cut practice time for them
rows.if: Goal is a `procedure` or `verbal-association` assessed on a standard test

rows.basis: [Multimodal, culturally grounded formative assessment supports engagement and agency](claims/multimodal-culturally-grounded-assessment-supports-engagement-and-agency.md) [+W] (youth aged 11–17 in two dance centres, researchers known to the sites; untested in a classroom with a new teacher)
rows.change: Accept movement, music and vernacular language as responses in formative checks, and say the check is a conversation
rows.if: Setting is informal or community-based (after-school, a community centre)

rows.basis: untested
rows.change: Give prompts that ask the learner to write their own example and explain the concept in it, with a bank of worked examples from several contexts; require no public sharing
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page's constraints (stereotyping, uneven familiarity)
rows.change: Use a private intake to collect contexts; draw examples from what learners wrote, not from assumptions about groups; offer several entry points per idea
rows.if: A large, mixed group, and the teacher does not know learners' communities

rows.basis: [Community projects need conceptual framing to avoid narrowing the learning object](claims/community-projects-need-conceptual-framing-to-avoid-narrowing-the-learning-object.md) [~W] (one case study)
rows.change: Name the concepts the project must use in advance, and hold a structured discussion with all groups midway about what the project means
rows.if: The design partners with a community organisation or local businesses

rows.basis: [Personal connection to data supports critical data-literacy stance-taking](claims/personal-connection-to-data-supports-critical-data-literacy-stance-taking.md) [~M] (prospective teachers; it occurred in all groups in one course and 1 of 6 in the other, tracking the instructor's framing)
rows.change: Plan explicit prompts that ask learners where they stand in what the data or text describes; do not expect personal connection to arise unprompted
rows.if: The instructor does not usually raise social or ethical questions in this course

rows.basis: [Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~M] (worked only where groups had opportunities to belong); [A brief values-affirmation writing exercise raised African American seventh-graders' grades in two small field experiments, but a large same-district replication found no effect](claims/self-affirmation-improves-outcomes.md) [~M] (a close replication found no benefit)
rows.change: Do not rely on one brief identity-related writing exercise; pair any belonging or values message with lasting structural support (check-ins, groups learners can join)
rows.if: Learners from groups stereotyped in the domain are at a transition (entry to a school, college or field) and stakes are high

rows.basis: untested
rows.change: Use one private prompt for a learner-supplied context and one explanation prompt; record what learners offer and claim nothing about lasting change
rows.if: Time is one session only

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page's constraints
rows.change: Make every personal prompt optional and private first; offer composite or fictional cases as equal alternatives; never ask a learner to represent a group
rows.if: Learners do not want to share personal experience (refugees, people in recovery, a mixed workplace)

rows.basis: Wait time: [Reviews of classroom studies, read from their abstracts, associate longer teacher wait time with longer, higher-cognitive-level student responses, with no effect size recorded](claims/increasing-wait-time-improves-response-quality.md) [+M] (reviews across grade levels, not by culture). Family conversation: untested
rows.change: Teach each convention by modelling and short practice ("now we think for three seconds, then whisper to your partner"); prefer choral and whiteboard response; talk with families about how questions and help work at home
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: Correction: [empathic discipline](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [+M] (US middle-school maths teachers). Rest untested
rows.change: Name conventions openly and invite learners to say where their norms differ; avoid public correction in front of peers; watch for learners who define themselves against school (step 10)
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent`

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Ask directly about expectations of hierarchy, questioning a trainer, and group versus individual credit; never treat silence as lack of knowledge; give written or private ways to raise a question
rows.if: Learners are `adult`, in `adult-workplace` or professional training

rows.basis: untested proposal; the wait-time reviews are of face-to-face classrooms
rows.change: Lengthen wait time further for remote learners (audio delay); take every whole-class answer through a poll or chat that both groups use; do not read camera-off or looking away as disengagement; call on remote learners only after a private check
rows.if: Mixed mode: some remote, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Leave response windows open rather than timed; give discussion-board options to post after reading others or to reply privately; state the platform's conventions on help and copying in plain terms
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: Wait time in classrooms: [Questioning Strategies Improve Learning](claims/questioning-strategies-improve-learning.md) [+M]. Tally and response modes: untested
rows.change: Use all-student response (cards, whiteboards, polls) for most questions and a simple tally of who answers publicly; correct conduct with low-profile moves first
rows.if: One teacher, a large class

rows.basis: Wait time: [Reviews of classroom studies, read from their abstracts, associate longer teacher wait time with longer, higher-cognitive-level student responses, with no effect size recorded](claims/increasing-wait-time-improves-response-quality.md) [+M]. The selection of three is untested
rows.change: Keep three moves only: three-second wait time, pair-before-share, and "ask before you name it" for conduct; skip the audit and arc
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time: volunteers, a busy shift, a tutor checking in briefly

rows.basis: Belonging boundary: [Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~M] (college entry). Rest untested
rows.change: State the session's conventions at the start (how to answer, how to ask for help, what counts as working together); use written or paired answers before any public one; do not run a one-off identity or belonging exercise and expect a lasting change
rows.if: A single session only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give private and oral options (tell a partner, then the partner reports), more wait time, no cold-calling until the learner has answered correctly in private
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or low literacy, or learning in a second language

rows.basis: [Questioning Strategies Improve Learning](claims/questioning-strategies-improve-learning.md) [+M] (higher-cognitive questions and wait time; not tested by culture)
rows.change: Choral and quick-fire response are fine for well-practised content; keep long wait time and pair talk for questions that need reasoning
rows.if: Goal is recall or fluency (`verbal-association`, `procedure`) rather than reasoning

rows.basis: [Cooperative Learning Improves Achievement](claims/cooperative-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+M]; [group rewards and individual accountability](claims/cooperative-learning-group-rewards-and-individual-accountability.md) [+M] (schools; not tested by culture)
rows.change: Add cooperative parts in which recognition rests on each member's individual learning; state before each task what help is allowed
rows.if: Grading or the activity is competitive and must stay so (curve, ranking, competitions)

rows.basis: [empathic discipline](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [+M] (US middle schools; the overall effect in the replication was marginal, the disparity effect larger)
rows.change: Give staff a brief empathic-discipline exercise and a "describe, ask, then act" routine; tally corrections by group each week; check that school policy does not undo it
rows.if: Discipline stakes are high (exclusion, suspension), or one group is corrected far more often

rows.basis: [Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~M]; [self-affirmation](claims/self-affirmation-improves-outcomes.md) [~M]; [teacher expectation effects](claims/teacher-expectation-effects-on-achievement.md) [~M] (one Dutch associational study)
rows.change: Change daily norms and the opportunities to belong before adding a brief belonging or affirmation exercise; ground judgements of ability in work samples, not in participation style
rows.if: Learners come from groups stereotyped as not belonging, or tracked low

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Rehearse in pairs or small groups first; offer a group presentation or a recorded one as well as a solo live one; agree in advance what questions the audience may ask
rows.if: A product or performance for a real audience (presentation, recital, pitch)

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Still run the audit and teach the conventions; diversity of class, religion, home language and schooling is usually present
rows.if: The class looks culturally homogeneous

rows.basis: Wait time: [Reviews of classroom studies, read from their abstracts, associate longer teacher wait time with longer, higher-cognitive-level student responses, with no effect size recorded](claims/increasing-wait-time-improves-response-quality.md) [+M]. Rest untested
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence says matters: at least three seconds of wait time inside it, one private or written answer before any public one, and a weekly check of who it calls on and who it corrects
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (its own participation protocol, cold-call policy, class charter or behaviour plan)

rows.basis: [Process goals lead to better skill acquisition for novices than outcome goals.](claims/process-goals-outperform-outcome-goals-for-novices.md) [+M] (high-school writing revision, carried to debrief focus); [Self Assessment Accuracy Is Low Without Training](claims/self-assessment-accuracy-is-low-without-training.md) [~M]
rows.change: Facilitator-led throughout; give the criterion or a model performance before analysis; ask about cues and steps, not outcomes; name what the expert would have noticed; one change each, stated as an action
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the task (first simulations, first placements)

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (cognitive-load studies; no study of debriefs)
rows.change: Learners choose the decision points and lead; the facilitator asks for alternatives considered and the reasoning behind them, and adds only what was missed; keep it shorter
rows.if: Learners are `advanced`, or experienced practitioners

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Five minutes, oral, teacher-led, three questions (what happened, what was tricky, what we will do next time), straight after the activity; one class change written on the board and read out next time
rows.if: Learners are `child`ren (primary age)

rows.basis: untested proposal; from the earlier page's examples
rows.change: Use an after-action format (what was planned, what happened, why the difference, what to keep and what to change); keep it separate from performance appraisal and from any incident investigation; write the changes into the team's next briefing
rows.if: `adult` learners in a work setting, after a real shift, project or incident

rows.basis: [Simulation Based Education With Deliberate Practice Improves Clinical Outcomes](claims/simulation-based-education-with-deliberate-practice-improves-clinical-outcomes.md) [+M] (14 studies, health professions); [Simulation Based Education Improves Outcomes](claims/simulation-based-education-improves-outcomes.md) [~M]: could not isolate feedback as the active feature
rows.change: Treat the debrief as the feedback step of a repeated attempt: debrief against a stated mastery standard, then rerun the scenario or a changed one until the standard is met
rows.if: Goal is a `procedure` or psychomotor skill in `workplace-clinical` training

rows.basis: [Prompting learners to self-explain…](claims/self-explanation-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+M] (immediate tests, study of examples and text; carried to debriefs)
rows.change: Spend most of the time on the learners' reasoning at two or three decision points; end with the general rule stated in the learner's words and tested on a new case
rows.if: Goal is judgement, a `concept` or a `principle` (diagnostic reasoning, a negotiation, an ethical decision)

rows.basis: untested proposal; from the earlier page's constraints
rows.change: Lengthen the reactions phase; check everyone is settled before analysis; move personal distress to a separate, private conversation; never analyse the performance of someone visibly upset in front of the group
rows.if: The experience was emotionally charged or high-stress

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Everyone writes their first answers (what happened, one decision point) in a shared chat or document before talking; the facilitator calls on remote learners first at each phase; share the recording or the timeline on screen; phone-only learners send a voice note or a two-line text
rows.if: Some learners join remotely while others are in the room, or some are on phones only

rows.basis: [Reflective Practice Improves Outcomes When Structured](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+M] (classroom engineering course); [Metacognitive prompts improve learning](claims/metacognitive-prompts-improve-learning.md) [+M] (computer-based environments)
rows.change: Replace the live debrief with a written self-debrief: three to five specific questions tied to the criteria, then a model performance or expert commentary to compare with, then one change for the next module, shown back at its start
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no facilitator

rows.basis: [Peer Discussion Improves Conceptual Understanding](claims/peer-discussion-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+M] (peers then instructor; undergraduate classes); peers who share a misconception may reinforce it, untested
rows.change: Debrief in threes or fours against a written protocol for 10 minutes; then the whole group on the most common gap, with the facilitator's explanation after the groups have reported
rows.if: One facilitator for a large group

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: A three-question debrief straight after, in five minutes: what happened at the key moment, one thing to keep, one change; the leader corrects any wrong rule in one sentence; changes go in a shared log; a full debrief only for critical or new events
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, a supervisor who can give five minutes)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: One short experience, a debrief of at least equal length, then a two-minute retry of the key moment with the change; do not claim retention
rows.if: One session only (`single-session`)

rows.basis: [Reflective Practice Improves Outcomes When Structured](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+M]; [Feedback Most Effective At Task And Process Levels](claims/feedback-most-effective-at-task-and-process-levels.md) [+S] (neither compares debrief models)
rows.change: Keep it. Check only that it reaches the learners' reasoning at specific decision points, gives task- and process-level feedback against a stated criterion, and ends with one written change for a next attempt; add whichever of those is missing as one question
rows.if: The brief names its own debrief model (plus/delta, PEARLS, GAS, an after-action review, the "What? So what? Now what?" questions)

rows.basis: [Feedback Most Effective At Task And Process Levels](claims/feedback-most-effective-at-task-and-process-levels.md) [+S] (feedback aimed at the self lost effect); separation from grading untested
rows.change: Separate the formative debrief from grading in time and by person where possible; talk about actions and decisions, never traits; record what was agreed, not who erred
rows.if: The performance is assessed or high-stakes, or the team must keep working together

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Debrief the team privately before any public review; use audience responses as evidence in the debrief, not as its verdict; keep the analysis out of anything the audience sees
rows.if: The product or performance was for a real audience (a public performance, a client deliverable, a community event)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Take first answers privately, orally or drawn, with sentence frames ("I saw…", "I decided… because…"); in the group, ask for actions, not explanations, from anyone not ready; judge the analysis, not the language
rows.if: Learners have low confidence or literacy, or speak in a second language

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (review of cognitive-load studies, carried to skill refinement); [process goals for novices](claims/process-goals-outperform-outcome-goals-for-novices.md) [~M]
rows.change: Do not isolate components yet: model the whole task, use guided practice with support, and set process goals; start targeted refinement only once the learner can perform unaided
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on this task, at first exposure

rows.basis: [Process goals lead to better skill acquisition for novices than outcome goals.](claims/process-goals-outperform-outcome-goals-for-novices.md) [~M] (reports that a shift to outcome goals after mastery can help; high-school writing)
rows.change: Let the learner pick the component from their own log, raise the standard, use outcome targets beside process goals, and give feedback mainly when the log shows a plateau
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` and have plateaued

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: The teacher chooses the component and writes the goal in the child's words; drills of five to ten minutes; a visible chart of attempts that met the standard; whole-task attempt at the end
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: [Deliberate practice and performance across domains](claims/deliberate-practice-improves-performance.md) [~M] (correlational meta-analysis: practice hours explain far more of performance in games, music and sports than in education or the professions; not a test of a design)
rows.change: Build the standard first: three or four annotated exemplars at different levels and a short rubric; expect smaller and slower gains than in sport or music, and check gains on new whole tasks
rows.if: Goal is a diffuse performance (`complex-skill` such as essay writing, teaching, leading a meeting)

rows.basis: [Simulation-based education with deliberate practice improves clinical outcomes](claims/simulation-based-education-with-deliberate-practice-improves-clinical-outcomes.md) [+M] (14 studies, health professions, procedural skills, against traditional clinical education)
rows.change: Use a simulator or part-task trainer with a mastery standard per step, immediate expert or device feedback, repetition until the standard is met and rising difficulty; add booster sessions later
rows.if: Goal is a `procedure` or psychomotor skill in `workplace-clinical` training

rows.basis: [Desirable difficulties enhance learning](claims/desirable-difficulties-enhance-learning.md) [~S] (spaced retrieval beats massed; interleaving helps some materials and not words); see [Retrieval Practice](principles/retrieval-practice.md)
rows.change: Use spaced retrieval practice with corrective feedback instead of component drills
rows.if: Goal is recall of facts or vocabulary (`verbal-association`)

rows.basis: [Self-monitoring improves self-regulation and supports better learning decisions.](claims/self-monitoring-improves-self-regulation.md) [+M] (reviews; untested within deliberate practice or online)
rows.change: Give items with automatic checking or a worked answer to compare; have the learner score against annotated exemplars and keep an error log; require one whole-task submission per session reviewed by a person or a rubric-based check
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, no coach present

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Work on the component most of the class misses; pairs score each other's attempts on that one rubric line; the teacher scans every whole-task attempt at the end and gives whole-class feedback on the commonest error
rows.if: `classroom` with one teacher and a large group

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: One component, three rounds of three to five attempts, then a scored whole-task attempt; report the change against the baseline as immediate only, not as retained
rows.if: Time is one session only

rows.basis: [Deliberate practice interventions produce higher real estate licensing exam pass rates](claims/deliberate-practice-raises-licensing-pass-rate.md) [+W] (one dissertation, two self-selected groups, no effect size)
rows.change: Choose components from an item analysis of practice exams, practice in the exam's format with feedback on each item, and run timed whole exams at intervals
rows.if: Stakes are high (licensing or certification exam)

rows.basis: untested; a practitioner assertion that over-challenge with too little support leads to giving up ([Imbalanced challenge and support causes novice library learners to give up or remain dependent](claims/challenge-support-imbalance-effects-novice-learners.md) [~W], no data)
rows.change: Shorten sessions, lower the step to the next standard, show the log of attempts that met it, and let the learner choose which component to work on next
rows.if: Learners are giving up, or the practice feels punitive

rows.basis: [Feedback improves learning by a medium amount on average, but its effect varies widely with the information it carries, and more than a third of feedback interventions reduce performance](claims/feedback-improves-learning.md) [~S] (more than a third of feedback interventions reduced performance, more so when they drew attention to the self; work and laboratory as well as education)
rows.change: Replace it with feedback about the attempt against the standard and the change to make next
rows.if: Feedback is mostly praise, grades or comparison with others

rows.basis: [Brief empathic-discipline exercise reduced suspensions](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [~S] (one targeted belief about discipline, middle-school mathematics teachers; carried to other decisions, untested); otherwise untested
rows.change: Run the scenario step (20–30 minutes), one group comparison of readings (15 minutes), and one written decision change with a named follow-up check (10 minutes); arrange for a peer tally or data review a few weeks later, even by email. Do not claim lasting change from the session
rows.if: A single session only (one workshop, one in-service hour)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Five minutes for one tally or data point, ten for one educator's case and the assumption it shows, five for each person's one changed decision; rotate whose data is discussed
rows.if: A fixed short time budget inside routine meetings (e.g. 20 minutes a month)

rows.basis: [Brief empathic-discipline exercise reduced suspensions](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [~S] (its Discussion notes a climate that rewards exclusion can erase gains [-W])
rows.change: Start with a reading of misbehaviour as a moment to keep the relationship, with a written reflection on how the educator would respond; track referrals or suspensions by group each term, and look at policies that require exclusion beside individual practice
rows.if: The decision is discipline, referrals or exclusion

rows.basis: untested here; [teacher expectation bias predicted later performance](claims/teacher-expectation-effects-on-achievement.md) [~M] is a reason to look (Dutch secondary cohort, associational)
rows.change: Use a peer tally or analytics of calls and praise by learner over one lesson, repeat after a named change; pair with the wait-time and private-response options in [Culturally Responsive Classroom Norms](principles/culturally-responsive-classroom-norms.md)
rows.if: The decision is who is called on, praised or corrected

rows.basis: [Teacher expectation bias predicted later performance](claims/teacher-expectation-effects-on-achievement.md) [~M] (associational; does not show that expectations cause the difference); [deficit perceptions are said to lower expectations](claims/deficit-view-of-minority-households-lowers-academic-expectations.md) [+W] (asserted, no evidence offered)
rows.change: Examine a sample of judgements against an independent measure (a common task scored blind); write explicit criteria before grading the next set
rows.if: The decision is expectations, grading or tracking

rows.basis: untested; household-research reports are from practising teachers ([funds of knowledge research raised teachers' expectations](claims/funds-of-knowledge-research-raises-teacher-expectations.md) [+W])
rows.change: Use more scenarios and other people's anonymised classrooms, fewer own-classroom tallies at first; include one visit or interview with a family or community member
rows.if: Educators are new or preservice

rows.basis: [Fluent illusions mislead self-assessment](claims/fluent-illusions-mislead-self-assessment.md) [~M] (adults judging their own learning in the laboratory; carried to judging one's own practice)
rows.change: Lead with their own tally rather than a discussion of bias; ask them to predict the tally first and compare
rows.if: Educators are experienced and confident they "treat everyone the same"

rows.basis: [Reflective study groups as a safe, non-judgemental place to think aloud](claims/teacher-researcher-difficulties-eased-by-reflective-labs.md) [~W] (one digest, teacher reports); otherwise untested
rows.change: Frame each session as examining decisions, not people; start with simulated cases; keep the naming of assumptions private for the first cycles and share only the changed decision
rows.if: Educators are defensive, or attendance is mandated

rows.basis: untested
rows.change: Use the workplace's own data (where staff come from, prior jobs, how names are read, first associations with nationalities and job titles), as in [stereotype-awareness activities for supervisors](strategies/stereotype-awareness-cultural-activities.md); the decision examined is allocation of tasks, feedback and promotion, tallied over a month
rows.if: Adults in work settings (supervisors, trainers of a diverse workforce)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Tally participation by channel (voice, chat, camera, in-room) as well as by learner; check who is addressed first and whose chat is answered; ask remote learners separately and anonymously
rows.if: Teaching is online, or mixed mode (some learners remote, some in the room; some on phones)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Pair educators to observe each other with a one-page tally; the facilitator reads only each pair's one-line summary and changed decision, and meets the group once per cycle
rows.if: One facilitator or coach for many educators, or scarce facilitator time (a busy term, volunteer coaches)

rows.basis: untested proposal; the external-evidence check rests on [fluent illusions mislead self-assessment](claims/fluent-illusions-mislead-self-assessment.md) [~M] (carried)
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence says matters: add one external data point to each cycle and require one named decision change with a follow-up check
rows.if: The brief names its own routine for this (its own observation protocol, reflection prompt, equity rubric or audit checklist)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Tally and review in those categories; do not substitute this page's examples
rows.if: The brief gives its own categories (the institution's learner groups, a district equity framework, the course team's audit headings)

rows.basis: untested proposal; from the earlier page's caution about defensiveness
rows.change: The educator controls who sees it: journals and assumption notes stay with the educator; the group sees only the tally and the changed decision; no grading of disclosures
rows.if: Reflection touches private or sensitive material (an educator's own identity, experiences of racism, journal entries about bias)

rows.basis: [Strength language often appeared without naming an actual strength](claims/coach-wright-topics-track-asset-deficit-mindsets.md) [~M] (simulation responses, associational)
rows.change: Assess decisions in a scenario (what the educator notices and would do) and changes in tallies, not attitudes or vocabulary; check that "strengths" language names an actual strength
rows.if: High stakes (required training, accreditation, a performance review)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Rehearse the whole conversation in a simulation or role play with debrief, rather than splitting it into knowledge items; record what the educator noticed and said
rows.if: The brief wants a whole difficult interaction rehearsed (a parent meeting, a disciplinary conversation, a complaint about bias)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Have members of that audience or community review examples, cases and images before release; record what they changed
rows.if: The product is materials or a course for a real audience

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding improves learning more than fixed or absent support.](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M] (one-to-one tutoring, carried to software)
rows.change: Use items close to worked examples, the full cue–hint–worked-step ladder, an explanation prompt every three to five items, and feedback on every item
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the task

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (a cognitive-load review; gives no crossover point)
rows.change: Remove most hints and prompts; give mixed, whole-task items and feedback only on request
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` on the task, or succeed unaided on the first set

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use short sessions (10 minutes or less), supervised by an adult in the room; give feedback that needs little reading; avoid open typed answers
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: untested proposal; contact task from [Online attrition during Orientation Week is twice that of onground classes' first week](claims/orientation-week-attrition-double-online.md) [~M] (university continuing education)
rows.change: Use short sets on a phone that can be done in one sitting, and tasks taken from their own work; keep the first-week contact task
rows.if: Learners are `adult` or professionals studying around work

rows.basis: [Adaptive learning improves outcomes](claims/adaptive-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+S] (tutoring-system meta-analyses; gains smaller on standardised than on locally developed tests)
rows.change: Put the bulk of practice online with automatic checking; use an intelligent tutor if one exists for the domain
rows.if: Goal is a `procedure` or `verbal-association` with checkable answers

rows.basis: [Prompting learners to self-explain improves understanding and problem solving on immediate tests by a moderate average amount, with little evidence yet on delayed or classroom gains.](claims/self-explanation-improves-conceptual-understanding.md) [+S] (not specific to digital delivery)
rows.change: Keep answer-checking, but add explanation prompts and changed items; hold discussion of reasons in a live or threaded session
rows.if: Goal is a `concept`, a `principle`, or transfer

rows.basis: [Self-regulated learning interventions have a moderate effect (0.65) on learning outcomes in online and blended environments](claims/srl-interventions-moderate-effect-online-blended.md) [+M] (15 studies); a diary alone did not help in one course ([A daily learning diary alone (Group D) did not produce statistically significant pre-post gains on any measured outcome in an online mathematics preparation course](claims/learning-diary-alone-no-significant-srl-gains-online-math-prep-course.md) [~M])
rows.change: Add the contact task in week 1, a fixed weekly rhythm with a deadline, visible progress against a criterion, and a weekly plan prompt; check logins by day 3
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: untested proposal; contingent-support evidence is one-to-one ([Contingent scaffolding improves learning more than fixed or absent support.](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M])
rows.change: Use the software for individual practice and hints while the teacher watches the class's results live and goes to those who are stuck; use class time for what the software cannot do (discussion of reasons, whole tasks)
rows.if: `classroom`, one teacher and a large group, devices available

rows.basis: untested proposal; learning a new interface costs time the method needs
rows.change: Do not introduce a new platform; use the classroom, or one familiar tool, for practice with feedback
rows.if: Time is short (one or two sessions)

rows.basis: [Laptop note-takers transcribed more verbatim and did worse on conceptual questions than longhand note-takers in one set of experiments, but a direct replication found no consistent difference in test performance](claims/laptop-notes-verbatim-shallower.md) [~M] (college students; a replication found no consistent difference)
rows.change: Ask learners to summarise in their own words, not transcribe; do not ban devices on the strength of the longhand evidence
rows.if: Note-taking during lectures on laptops or tablets is planned

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Judge readiness only on unaided items done without hints; keep a log of hints used; give at least one supervised check in the final assessment's format
rows.if: Stakes are high, or the final assessment is unaided and supervised

rows.basis: untested proposal, from the earlier page
rows.change: Make every required activity available offline or on paper, use low-bandwidth formats (text, short audio, captioned video), and grade nothing that some learners cannot reach
rows.if: Access is uneven (shared devices, poor bandwidth, accessibility needs)

rows.basis: [Graphic organizers for novices](claims/graphic-organizers-support-novice-comprehension.md) [~M] (lower-ability learners benefited from maps, higher-ability did not, in small, low-powered subsets)
rows.change: Supply a complete, labelled visual first, with linking prompts; give construction only as a partly completed diagram
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on this content

rows.basis: [Graphic organizers for novices](claims/graphic-organizers-support-novice-comprehension.md) [~M] (the higher-ability subset showed no benefit; the authors say this cannot show maps fail them); the redraw is untested
rows.change: Drop most supplied visuals; ask for a redraw from memory or a learner-made summary diagram, checked against a model
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` on this content

rows.basis: Supplied: [text with graphics](claims/dual-coding-improves-learning.md) [+M] (effect held across grade levels). Drawing: [drawing in STEM](claims/drawing-improves-learning.md) [~M] (benefit larger in middle and high school than in primary)
rows.change: Supply pictures and flow diagrams with the text; have children label or complete them rather than draw freely
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: [Drawing in STEM](claims/drawing-improves-learning.md) [+M] (STEM only, abstract read)
rows.change: Add learner drawing of the process or system, with a model to compare against
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent` or `adult`, goal is a `principle` in science or mathematics

rows.basis: L2: [text-plus-picture glosses](claims/multimodal-glosses-improve-incidental-vocabulary-learning.md) [+W] (one study of 90 Iranian EFL learners, immediate recall, reported second-hand). Disabilities: [mnemonic instruction](claims/mnemonic-instruction-improves-recall-for-students-with-disabilities.md) [+M] (mnemonics broadly, not only pictorial ones)
rows.change: Pair each new word with a picture and a short text gloss; for students with learning disabilities, teach a keyword-image mnemonic
rows.if: Goal is `verbal-association` (vocabulary, names, facts), including second-language vocabulary

rows.basis: [Concept mapping](claims/concept-mapping-improves-learning.md) [+M] (STEM and non-STEM; constructing showed more benefit than studying, against different comparisons)
rows.change: Have learners build and revise a concept map across sessions, with labelled links, starting from given nodes
rows.if: Goal is a `concept` or hierarchy to be understood across a unit

rows.basis: [Drawing in STEM](claims/drawing-improves-learning.md) [+M] (online drawing benefited more from instructor-provided scaffolds than paper-based drawing)
rows.change: Build drawing templates, a model drawing to compare with, and a self-check list into the material
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: [Concept mapping against retrieval](claims/concept-mapping-improves-learning.md) [~M] (undergraduates, science text, time matched, one-week test)
rows.change: Keep the supplied visual; replace building a map while viewing with redrawing or explaining it from memory
rows.if: Little time, or the goal is recall a week later

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Collect a sample of learner drawings each session, show one correct and one common error to the class, then have everyone compare their own with the model
rows.if: Large class, one teacher

rows.basis: [Verbal tests may underestimate knowledge](claims/verbal-achievement-tests-may-underestimate-via-symbolic-mismatch.md) [~W] (an argument in a review, not a tested result); [text with graphics](claims/dual-coding-improves-learning.md) [+M] (larger effect on open-ended items)
rows.change: Include items that ask for a diagram or a prediction from one; decide whether the visual may be consulted
rows.if: Assessment is high-stakes or verbal only

rows.basis: [Learning-styles matching](claims/learning-styles-matching-does-not-improve-learning.md) [-S] (systematic review; 5th graders showed no style × modality interaction)
rows.change: Give the visual to every learner where the content has a visual structure; do not sort learners or build matched versions
rows.if: The brief describes "visual learners" or asks for materials matched to learning styles

rows.basis: [Decorative illustrations](claims/decorative-illustrations-do-not-improve-learning.md) [-M] (no learning gain; a small comprehension cost for undergraduates, η² = .04)
rows.change: Keep only images that show what the words describe; if an image must stay for branding, keep it away from the explanatory visual
rows.if: The designer wants images for appeal or engagement

rows.basis: [Universal classroom management](claims/universal-classroom-management-reduces-problem-behavior.md) [+M] and [less disruption in all 12 studies](claims/treatment-classrooms-less-disruptive-than-control.md) [+M] (K–12 classrooms, against usual practice)
rows.change: Start with steps 1 and 2: re-teach every routine for two weeks, with daily rehearsal, before adding any new consequence; tally disruptions before and after
rows.if: The whole class is disruptive

rows.basis: untested here; see [Functional Behavior Assessment](principles/functional-behavior-assessment.md)
rows.change: Keep the class plan; start an individual assessment of what triggers and keeps up each learner's behavior
rows.if: One or two learners cause most incidents despite the plan

rows.basis: untested proposal; the meta-analysis covers K–12 without an age breakdown
rows.change: Fewer rules (three), shown with pictures; routines rehearsed physically and daily for longer (four to six weeks); immediate, frequent praise; redirection by proximity and a quiet prompt, not warnings; no self-recording yet
rows.if: Learners are a young `child` (preschool or early primary)

rows.basis: [Greetings at the door](claims/positive-greetings-at-the-door-improve-engagement.md) [+M] (middle-school classes); [self-monitoring](claims/self-monitoring-improves-on-task-behavior.md) [+M] (grades 4–12, students with or at risk for disabilities); the rest untested
rows.change: Agree the rules with the class in the first week; give reasons for every procedure; greet each learner at the door; correct in private, never in front of peers; add self-recording for learners who want it
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent`s who meet many teachers a day

rows.basis: untested proposal; no claim here tests adult groups
rows.change: Replace rules with a short working agreement drafted with the group in the first session (phones, start times, how to disagree); keep the routines for materials, breaks and getting help; handle problems in a private conversation; drop rewards and the consequence ladder
rows.if: Learners are `adult`s in a work setting, adult education or training

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Make every routine work in both: one attention signal that shows on screen and in the room, a named way to ask for help in each (raised hand, chat, a direct message), greet remote learners by name at the start; keep cameras optional and correct remote learners only by private message
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners online, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: untested proposal; the greeting claim is from middle-school doorways, carried to an online join it did not test
rows.change: Turn the routines into written norms posted at the top of each session (mute, chat use, breakout rooms, when to use cameras); greet each learner by name as they join; scan the participant list as you would the room
rows.if: Online class only (`online-instructor-led`)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Rely on prevention and routines more than on individual redirection: a visible attention signal, short timed tasks with a clear start and end, a routine for asking for help without the teacher, and peer roles for materials; respond to the group, then to individuals after class
rows.if: One teacher with a large group (a lecture, a large class, no assistant)

rows.basis: [Greetings at the door](claims/positive-greetings-at-the-door-improve-engagement.md) [+M], carried to a single session it did not test; the rest untested
rows.change: Do not build a plan; state three expectations at the start, greet each learner, use the host's existing routines where you know them, redirect with the least intrusive move, and leave a short note on what happened for the regular teacher
rows.if: A single session only (cover teacher, a one-off workshop, a guest)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Fit the routines to the minutes: in a ten-minute budget, two minutes of greeting and start-up, one routine rehearsed for three minutes, and the rest left for the attention signal and transitions; in a single workshop, a two-minute agreement at the start and one attention signal
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (for example ten minutes a lesson for management, or a two-hour workshop)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Cut the plan to one page: three expectations, one attention signal, one help routine and one consequence; give every adult the same page so learners meet the same responses; one named person reviews a weekly tally for five minutes
rows.if: Scarce adult time (volunteers, a busy shift, one tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: untested proposal; see [Check In Check Out](strategies/check-incheck-out.md) and [Good Behavior Game](strategies/good-behavior-game.md); rewards: [expected tangible rewards](claims/rewards-undermine-intrinsic-motivation.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep it and its categories; change only what the evidence says matters: teach and rehearse its expectations rather than only posting them, apply its consequences the same way every time, add a greeting, and write down when any tangible reward in it will be thinned
rows.if: The brief names its own routine or system (a school behavior policy, a schoolwide expectations matrix, a class points chart, check-in/check-out, the Good Behavior Game)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use its wording as the rules; build the routines and the ladder around those categories rather than adding a new set
rows.if: The brief gives its own rules, criteria or rubric for behavior

rows.basis: [Expected tangible rewards](claims/rewards-undermine-intrinsic-motivation.md) [-M] (meta-analyses of mostly laboratory tasks; stronger for children in one)
rows.change: Use specific praise and the activity's own payoff instead; keep tangible rewards for tasks learners find dull, tied to a standard, with a date for thinning them
rows.if: The plan relies on prizes or points for activities learners already enjoy

rows.basis: [Empathic discipline](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [+M] (middle-school teachers; narrowed a racial suspension disparity in the preregistered replication); norms: [Culturally Responsive Classroom Norms](principles/culturally-responsive-classroom-norms.md)
rows.change: Review who is corrected and excluded, by group, every two weeks; widen the participation and correction norms; read departures as possible differences of convention first; offer staff the empathic-discipline exercise
rows.if: Learners' cultural norms differ from the classroom's, or one group receives most corrections

rows.basis: [Empathic discipline](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [+M] (overall effect small and marginal; larger for previously suspended students)
rows.change: Show the tally and who is being excluded; agree a short consistent ladder in advance; keep consequences that repair rather than shame
rows.if: Staff or the school want harsher punishment or exclusion

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do not display individual behavior charts or names publicly; keep tallies at class level on the wall and individual records with the teacher and the learner (and family, where a school requires it); let older learners keep their own self-recording sheet
rows.if: Behavior records are private or sensitive (individual charts, notes on a learner)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Show rules and routines as pictures, gestures and demonstrations, not text; rehearse rather than explain; give a non-verbal help signal; never use reading aloud or public answering as a consequence
rows.if: Learners with low literacy, a language barrier or low confidence

rows.basis: [Self-monitoring](claims/self-monitoring-improves-on-task-behavior.md) [+M] (single-case studies; on-task behavior, not achievement)
rows.change: Add self-recording of on-task behavior at prompted intervals for those who need it, with brief training; keep the class routines the same for everyone
rows.if: Learners with or at risk for disabilities in the class

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the performance whole; put the routines around it: a safety and equipment routine rehearsed beforehand, a single stop signal everyone obeys at once, roles for each learner, and redirection that does not stop the performance
rows.if: A practical, rehearsal or performance for a real audience (a lab, a workshop, a concert, a public presentation) that the brief wants kept whole

rows.basis: [Coaching increases teacher praise](claims/coaching-increases-teacher-praise.md) [+W] (a review of coaching studies; teacher behavior, not student outcomes); student-side effects are mixed: [supervisory coaching](claims/supervisory-coaching-mixed-teacher-student-outcomes.md) [~W]
rows.change: Give the teacher the one-page plan, a short ladder and a coach who observes and gives feedback on praise and redirection in the room
rows.if: A new or inexperienced teacher, or one with few strategies

rows.basis: [Process goals lead to better skill acquisition for novices than outcome goals.](claims/process-goals-outperform-outcome-goals-for-novices.md) [~M] (high-school writing revision); the step-size move is untested
rows.change: Shorten steps, give a worked example first, set process goals; do not add hooks or rewards
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the task and withdraw after early failure

rows.basis: [Expected tangible rewards reduce later free-choice engagement with a rewarded task, while verbal praise does not](claims/rewards-undermine-intrinsic-motivation.md) [~S] (one meta-analysis reports rewards more detrimental for children than college students); block lengths untested
rows.change: Keep the arrival routine, short work blocks, teacher-held progress chart; avoid tangible rewards for taking part
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: [Positive Greetings At The Door Improve Engagement](claims/positive-greetings-at-the-door-improve-engagement.md) [+M] (middle school); [Self Monitoring Improves On Task Behavior](claims/self-monitoring-improves-on-task-behavior.md) [+M] (students with or at risk for disabilities; carried to others untested)
rows.change: Add the greeting routine at every lesson; for individual learners, cued self-recording of on-task behaviour in work blocks
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent`, with disruptive or off-task behaviour

rows.basis: [Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [+M] (first-year college students; worked only where the institution afforded belonging)
rows.change: Before or at the start of the course, a short exercise in which learners read and write about adversity as common and temporary; check that the setting gives them real opportunities to belong
rows.if: Learners are `adult` or in their first year of college, unsure they belong

rows.basis: [Constructive learning beats active and passive learning](claims/constructive-learning-beats-active-passive.md) [~M] (ordering only partly held in the field)
rows.change: Judge success by an explanation or prediction probe, not by on-task time; make the engaged task one of explaining or predicting
rows.if: Goal is a `concept` or `principle`, measured by `conceptual-understanding`

rows.basis: [Learners invest more effort in tasks they perceive as interesting, personally important, or useful to their future goals.](claims/task-value-increases-motivation-and-engagement.md) [+M] (reviews; utility-value effects reported second-hand)
rows.change: Measure voluntary return or later course choice, not enjoyment ratings at the end of a session; use relevance writing at unit starts
rows.if: The goal is `attitude-motivation` itself (interest in a subject, continued study)

rows.basis: untested; [Intervention engagement (narratives consumed) showed no clear association with outcome changes](claims/story-mine-engagement-outcome-null-association.md) [~W] warns that usage counts need not track outcomes (a mental-health app, not learning)
rows.change: Replace the greeting with a named welcome and first-minute check-in; build a visible progress record and automatic learning checks; track return days, not only clicks
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: [Interesting but irrelevant details can impair comprehension and transfer, with effects that vary with the material and the learner](claims/seductive-details-effect.md) [-M] (school and university learners; harm larger for low prior knowledge or low attentional inhibition)
rows.change: Keep only additions that show the target idea; place any purely motivating story before or after the core explanation
rows.if: Materials are being "made more engaging" with images, stories, jokes or video

rows.basis: [Gamification has small positive effects on cognitive, motivational and behavioral learning outcomes](claims/gamification-has-small-positive-effects-on-learning-outcomes.md) [~M]; [rewards](claims/rewards-undermine-intrinsic-motivation.md) [~S]
rows.change: Use them only alongside a task that requires thinking with the target; do not give tangible rewards merely for taking part; measure learning separately
rows.if: The plan relies on points, badges, leaderboards or prizes

rows.basis: untested at scale; the greeting claim is from middle-school classrooms ([greetings](claims/positive-greetings-at-the-door-improve-engagement.md) [+M])
rows.change: Make participation visible all at once (everyone writes or shows a response); use spot checks of on-task behaviour across the room; greet at the door even if briefly
rows.if: `classroom` with one teacher and a large group

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use the reason-for-task and a constructive task; do not claim durable engagement; record one learning probe
rows.if: Time is one session, or a one-off workshop

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep relevance and progress supports; do not let engagement indicators stand in for evidence of competence
rows.if: Stakes are high (assessed course, certification)

rows.basis: [Positive teacher–student relationships are associated with greater student engagement and, more weakly, with achievement](claims/teacher-student-relationships-improve-engagement.md) [+M] (correlational; direction not established)
rows.change: Start with the contact routine and warm, high-expectation feedback before adding choice or open tasks
rows.if: Relationship with the group is new or strained

rows.basis: [Elementary students prefer mechanistic explanations](claims/elementary-students-prefer-mechanistic-explanations.md) [+W]: grades 2–6, observed in interviews, no instruction tested
rows.change: Frame questions as "how does it happen?" and have learners compare a mechanistic and a non-mechanistic explanation of a familiar phenomenon, giving a reason; keep content to what they already know, since they reject explanations that conflict with their knowledge. Do not expect web-source evaluation routines to transfer down.
rows.if: `child` learners (primary school)

rows.basis: [Civic Online Reasoning Instruction Improves Evaluation](claims/civic-online-reasoning-instruction-improves-evaluation.md) [+M]: high-school field study, matched controls
rows.change: Embed six 50-minute lessons on lateral reading in an existing subject (government, history), with teacher preparation; practise on live sites.
rows.if: `adolescent` learners, web or news sources, a school course

rows.basis: [Collaborative critique-and-redesign](claims/collaborative-evidence-critique-shifts-students-toward-procedural-objectivity.md) [+M]: first-year psychology, single group, no control
rows.change: Run small-group critique and redesign of flawed studies in the discipline across the course (three tasks in a 12-week course), and teach credibility of sources separately if it is also a goal.
rows.if: `adult` learners, university, judging research

rows.basis: [Collaborative critique-and-redesign](claims/collaborative-evidence-critique-shifts-students-toward-procedural-objectivity.md) [~M]: no change on the untaught lay-credibility judgments
rows.change: Name the specific judgments it should show up in and teach and assess each; do not assume one transfers to another.
rows.if: Goal is a general disposition ("critical thinking", "scepticism")

rows.basis: [Argumentation Improves Reasoning](claims/argumentation-improves-reasoning.md) [+M]: multi-year study with young adolescents; online-science synthesis
rows.change: Use repeated peer argument on contested questions, followed by individual essays on new topics; plan for many sessions, not one.
rows.if: Goal is writing or arguing a case with evidence

rows.basis: [Checklist-based evaluation](claims/checklist-evaluation-ineffective-online.md) [~M]: one-session checklist and networked framework did not differ; gains modest
rows.change: Teach one move (leave the page and search what others say about the source) rather than a long checklist, and expect modest gains; schedule a follow-up task if at all possible.
rows.if: Only one session (e.g. a library visit)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the online-argumentation synthesis does not report teacher presence
rows.change: Provide recorded demonstrations of the expert move, live practice items with model reasoning shown after the learner commits a judgment and a confidence rating, and a delayed check on new items.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: Untested proposal; one nursing study is single-session and is read in the checklist row
rows.change: Use the claims they will meet at work (health websites, research summaries); teach both source checking and study-method judgments if both occur, and assess each.
rows.if: `workplace-clinical` learners (e.g. nurses judging health information)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; constructed-response and five-week tests appear in the lateral-reading studies
rows.change: Assess with constructed responses on unseen claims, scoring the reason and the verdict, at a delay; a multiple-choice verdict alone can be right for the wrong reason.
rows.if: High-stakes assessment of the skill

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the lateral-reading claim's discussion names the constraint, no study tests it
rows.change: Lateral reading cannot be practised as such; supply a curated packet of outside documents about each source and teach the learner to look for them, or shift the target to judging the reasoning inside the source.
rows.if: No open web access, locked devices, or offline exam

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Do not open with errors. Teach or show one or two correct worked examples first; add one erroneous example per misconception only once the learner can follow a correct one.
rows.if: `novice`: no correct model of this task yet

rows.basis: [productive failure](claims/productive-failure-improves-conceptual-learning.md) [~M]; [overt correction for young children](claims/overt-error-correction-speeds-young-children-learning.md) [~W] (second-hand, 1962 study)
rows.change: Keep correction overt (show the correct answer and how, not only right/wrong); use constructed peer errors after instruction rather than problem-first failure, which reversed for second to fifth graders.
