rows.if: The brief sets its own criteria or rubric for discussion quality

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Fit it: week 1, 10 minutes for introductions and two replies; later weeks, 5 minutes for one named reply in the small group and 5 for reading the instructor's weekly message; one live meeting a month only if time allows
rows.if: A fixed short time budget for community work (say 10 minutes a week)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Build presence inside the project: a kickoff meeting where members introduce what they bring, agreed roles, and regular short live check-ins; do not split the project into individual posting quotas
rows.if: The course ends in a group product or performance for a real audience, or a whole-task project the brief wants kept whole

rows.basis: [Human embodiment in video](claims/human-embodiment-video-presence-effects.md) [~M] (second-hand review; perceived learning higher with the instructor's face, performance not different)
rows.change: Put effort into replies, weekly named messages and live contact rather than into the instructor's face in every content video
rows.if: The course is pre-recorded video and the budget goes on production

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Grade the substance of contributions against stated criteria, never personal disclosure or post counts; keep social spaces ungraded
rows.if: High stakes for the learner, or participation is graded

rows.basis: [SAT underpredicts girls' performance](claims/sat-underpredicts-girls-performance.md) [~W]; [National Merit awards skew male](claims/psat-national-merit-awards-skew-male.md) [~W] (both 1987 testimony, second-hand); the directions by group are the earlier page's (Young 2004)
rows.change: Add a second piece of evidence (grades, a work sample) for every applicant within a band of the cut; run a differential-prediction check once first-year outcomes are in, and do not assume which direction any gap runs
rows.if: The score gates admission or a scholarship with a single cut-off

rows.basis: [Culturally and linguistically diverse students under-identified nationwide](claims/gifted-underrepresentation-diverse-students.md) [~W] and [teachers under-refer them](claims/teacher-underreferral-diverse-gifted.md) [~W] (one issue brief); [a narrative review attributes under-representation to biased measures](claims/culturally-diverse-underrepresentation-biased-measures.md) [~W] (second-hand, Ford 2003); [traditional identification tests omit classroom-learning components](claims/traditional-identification-tests-fail-learning-potential.md) [~W] (argument). None tests universal screening or multiple measures
rows.change: Screen every learner rather than relying on teacher referral; use more than one measure, including a performance or classroom-learning measure; compare each group's identification rate with its share of enrolment every year
rows.if: The decision is gifted or enrichment identification

rows.basis: Untested in the wiki (stereotype threat has no claim page); affirmation: [raised grades in two small trials, null in a large replication](claims/self-affirmation-improves-outcomes.md) [~M] (seventh graders, term grades, not test scores)
rows.change: Move demographic questions to after the test; describe the test by its use, not as a measure of ability; consider a values-affirmation exercise only as a measured trial
rows.if: Learners belong to a group negatively stereotyped in the tested domain (women in mathematics; Black or Latino students in academic tests) and the sitting is high-stakes

rows.basis: [Math anxiety degrades performance](claims/math-anxiety-degrades-performance.md) [~M] (meta-analysis of correlations; does not test these moves); [higher anxiety goes with smaller testing effects](claims/higher-anxiety-is-associated-with-smaller-testing-effects.md) [~M] (retrieval practice, review chapter)
rows.change: Two or three untimed, then timed, practice sittings in the real format with feedback; ask the test owner whether extended time is allowed; read a single timed high-stakes score with caution
rows.if: Learners are anxious about tests, or the test is timed and speed is not the construct

rows.basis: [Verbal tests may underestimate subject knowledge](claims/verbal-achievement-tests-may-underestimate-via-symbolic-mismatch.md) [~W] (argument); [minority-testing research has rarely examined alternative symbolic forms](claims/minority-testing-research-neglects-alternative-symbolic-forms.md) [~W] (a 1986 review noting the gap)
rows.change: Use the accommodations the test allows (glossaries, read-aloud for non-reading tests, extra time); do not read a low score as low subject knowledge without a second, low-language measure; for items you write, keep reading load below the construct
rows.if: Learners are taking the test in a second language, or have low literacy

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do not use one sitting for a placement; observe over several occasions; use pictures and spoken instructions; re-screen within the year
rows.if: Learners are young children (`child`) taking a screening or readiness test

rows.basis: [ICC and LDF methods flag different items](claims/icc-and-ldf-methods-identify-different-dif-items.md) [~M]; [item purification flags more items](claims/item-purification-increases-dif-detection-sensitivity.md) [~M]; [NC-DIF chi-square over-sensitive at large n](claims/nc-dif-chi-square-overly-sensitive-large-samples.md) [~M] (simulation, attributed to Fleer 1993); [male-oriented item content](claims/male-oriented-item-content-biases-test-scores.md) [~W]
rows.change: Content review by reviewers from varied backgrounds, then DIF with at least two methods on large samples; every flagged item gets a content review before it is dropped; record which method flagged it
rows.if: You write or own the items (a district, an awarding body, an assessment product)

rows.basis: untested proposal; DIF Type I error rates rose with more and larger DIF items in simulation ([DIF Type I error increases with DIF items and magnitude](claims/dif-type-i-error-increases-with-dif-items-and-magnitude.md) [~M]), so small or contaminated samples give unstable flags
rows.change: Skip DIF and regression statistics for now; rely on content review and on second evidence near the cut; pool several years before running them
rows.if: Groups are small (a single school or programme, under about 100 per group)

rows.basis: [Later-positioned item more difficult](claims/later-position-item-more-difficult-fatigue-effect.md) [~M]; [DIF items differently positioned across booklets](claims/dif-items-differently-positioned-across-booklets.md) [~M] (one national examination)
rows.change: Keep item positions fixed across forms, or check each item's difficulty by position before comparing groups who took different forms
rows.if: Several forms or booklets are used

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give the same items, time and aids, or record the difference beside each score; avoid long passages and wide tables on phones; compare score distributions by mode before pooling, and check that mode is not standing in for a group (rural, low-income)
rows.if: The test is taken in mixed modes: some in a centre, some remote, some on phones only

rows.basis: untested proposal; the prediction check (step 3) applied to a job criterion
rows.change: Check that the items sample the job's tasks, not general reading or cultural knowledge; validate the score against observed job performance by group; add a work-sample task for candidates near the cut
rows.if: Adults in work settings: a licensing, promotion or job-entry test

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use one full practice sitting under real conditions, self-marked against an answer key with worked reasons, and spend the scarce contact time only on the three items most learners missed; move demographic forms after the test, which needs no time
rows.if: One teacher or tutor prepares many learners, or facilitator time is scarce (volunteers, a short weekly session)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use it for one timed practice in the real format with immediate feedback and a walk-through of the instructions; do not add new content
rows.if: Only a single session is available before the real test

rows.basis: untested; the three changes follow the three mechanisms above
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence here says matters: no single-score cut without a second look near it, demographics after the test, and a by-group check of who is selected and how they later do
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (its own admissions rubric, test-prep programme, identification checklist)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Report by group with the number of test-takers and the uncertainty; do not compare groups on a score whose prediction has not been checked for them; link the use to [High-Stakes Testing and Accountability Effects](principles/high-stakes-testing-accountability-effects.md)
rows.if: Results are reported publicly or drive accountability (school league tables, programme funding)

rows.basis: [Teacher expectation bias predicted Dutch secondary students' performance up to five years later, after controls for prior achievement, IQ and motivation, in one large correlational cohort study](claims/teacher-expectation-effects-on-achievement.md) [+M] (correlational, Dutch secondary cohort; not a test of intervening on expectations); [Teachers underrefer culturally and linguistically diverse students for gifted identification](claims/teacher-underreferral-diverse-gifted.md) [+W] (a brief summarising referral research)
rows.change: Collect strengths from a new low-stakes task in several response modes before reading the file; write barriers and supports beside them; set at least one task above the level the label implies
rows.if: Learners have been labeled (disability, special educational needs, "low ability" set) or have a record of failure

rows.basis: [Assessment tasks built on family-identified funds of knowledge elicited computational thinking from K-2 children in a small design-based study that made no comparison with standard assessment](claims/funds-of-knowledge-tasks-reveal-computational-thinking.md) [+M] (K-2, 13 children, no comparison); [Praise for intelligence, rather than for effort, after success undermines children's motivation and performance after a later failure](claims/feedback-praise-reduces-learning.md) [-S] (fifth graders, intelligence praise)
rows.change: Collect strengths through families and play-based tasks built from home practices; name strengths aloud as what the child did, never as "smart"; keep the self-record oral or pictorial
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: Adults: untested proposal. Feedback channel: [The effect of social persuasion on student teacher efficacy depends on its form](claims/social-persuasion-form-moderates-efficacy-effect.md) [~M] (student teachers, reported in a review: verbal feedback from the cooperating teacher related to efficacy; a structured rating tool was detrimental against a control)
rows.change: Ask what they already do at work that the course builds on, and use those tasks as entry points; feedback comes from the supervisor or mentor in person, naming a specific performance, rather than through a rating form
rows.if: Learners are `adult` in work settings (trainees, career changers, professionals)

rows.basis: [Proximal goals and ability attributional feedback for early learning raise self-efficacy more than distant goals and effort feedback, by a review's report of earlier studies](claims/proximal-goals-feedback-peer-models-build-learning-efficacy.md) [+M] (review of experiments, second-hand); [Learners' task-specific self-efficacy beliefs predict…](claims/self-efficacy-predicts-academic-persistence.md) [+M] (narrative reviews)
rows.change: Shorten the first tasks so success comes early and is genuine; credit early success to the learner's own skill and strategy; set close-at-hand goals; never give praise that the learner can see is unearned
rows.if: Learners have low confidence after repeated failure in this subject

rows.basis: untested proposal; from the earlier page (multilingual learners, interrupted education)
rows.change: Let learners show a strength in their home language, by demonstration or drawing; record it; teach the academic register explicitly as the next target, not as the measure of the strength
rows.if: Learners are multilingual or have low literacy in the language of instruction

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Replace individual conferences with a written two-line strengths-and-next-target comment on one piece of work per learner per fortnight, and a learner self-record checked at the same time; use the low-stakes task in step 1 for everyone in the first week
rows.if: `classroom` with one teacher and a large group

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Build the strengths record into the platform: a short self-report on what has worked, and feedback that names the specific item the learner got right and the next item it unlocks; keep each entry to a few lines
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, or learners work on phones only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Collect strengths from submitted work and the chat as well as from talk in the room, so remote learners are not judged only by what the teacher hears; hold the strengths conference one-to-one by call
rows.if: Some learners join remotely while others are in the room

rows.basis: [Growth-mindset interventions have weak average effects on achievement, including a negligible GPA gain (d = 0.11) for lower-achieving US ninth-graders in one preregistered national trial](claims/growth-mindset-improves-achievement.md) [~S] (a brief online intervention moved ninth graders' GPA by a negligible amount; meta-analyses weak overall); carried from mindset messages to strengths framing
rows.change: Give one low-stakes task, then one piece of specific feedback naming what worked and a next target; do not run a mindset or encouragement talk in place of it, and claim nothing about lasting change
rows.if: Time is one session only

rows.basis: untested proposal; [Teachers underrefer culturally and linguistically diverse students for gifted identification](claims/teacher-underreferral-diverse-gifted.md) [+W] for the referral check
rows.change: Judge readiness on the standard task, not on the familiar-form task; record both; for referral or placement, use step 1's evidence to check that learners are not left out because of how they show competence
rows.if: Stakes are high (certification, placement, gifted referral)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Assign production roles from recorded strengths for the first product, rotate them for the next; name to each learner which part of the finished product shows their strength
rows.if: Learners produce work for a real audience (a performance, a product, a client)

rows.basis: [A brief values-affirmation writing exercise raised African American seventh-graders' grades in two small field experiments, but a large same-district replication found no effect](claims/self-affirmation-improves-outcomes.md) [~S]; [Growth-mindset interventions have weak average effects on achievement, including a negligible GPA gain (d = 0.11) for lower-achieving US ninth-graders in one preregistered national trial](claims/growth-mindset-improves-achievement.md) [~S]
rows.change: Keep it, if at all, as a small complement placed before a high-stakes moment; put the design effort into feedback, task entry points and support
rows.if: A brief belief exercise (values affirmation, mindset lesson) is proposed as the strengths component

rows.basis: [Specific, difficult goals lead to higher performance than easy or vague "do your best" goals.](claims/specific-difficult-goals-lead-to-higher-performance.md) [~M] (one narrative review, adult task performance; carried to classrooms)
rows.change: Little framing is needed: name strengths briefly and spend the time on harder, specific goals
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` on the task, or already confident

rows.basis: [Classroom quizzing delivered by clickers, computer software, or paper improves student performance on classroom exams in middle school and college courses](claims/classroom-quizzing-improves-exam-performance-across-grades-and-content.md) [+M] for quizzing during the course; the practice run itself is untested
rows.change: Add a full practice run in the end-point's format a week before, with worked answers; keep the first summative of the course lower in weight
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the format (first exam of this kind, first-year students, a new kind of task)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Judge over several short occasions and observed work rather than one long test; read questions aloud where reading is not the outcome
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: untested proposal; threshold decisions are held by [Competency-Based Assessment](principles/competency-based-assessment.md)
rows.change: Make the end-point a task from their work, observed or produced on the job, judged against a stated competency threshold; ask what they already do and test only what is new
rows.if: Learners are `adult` professionals, or in `adult-workplace` training

rows.basis: [A training-design argument, not tested by any study recorded here, holds that practising whole complex tasks improves transfer of complex skills](claims/whole-task-performance-improves-transfer.md) [~W] (an argument about training, carried here to assessment)
rows.change: Include a whole-task performance, scored with a rubric, plus short component items so a failure can be traced to a part
rows.if: Goal is a `complex-skill` (a design, a case, a clinical or practical performance)

rows.basis: [University examination questions concentrate at the lower cognitive levels of Bloom's Taxonomy, dominated by comprehension and knowledge](claims/exam-questions-concentrate-lower-bloom-levels.md) [~M]; [Students perform better overall on LOCS exam questions than on HOCS exam questions](claims/locs-exam-questions-outperform-hocs.md) [~M]; [HOCS clicker questions during learning improve performance on LOCS exam questions more than LOCS clicker questions do](claims/hocs-clickers-improve-locs-exam-performance.md) [+M] (one nonmajors biology course)
rows.change: Blueprint the paper so those levels carry marks; expect lower scores on them and practise them in class beforehand
rows.if: Outcomes ask for analysis, evaluation or creation, not only recall

rows.basis: [In one community-college lab class, six scorers rating six teams with an engineering rubric differed by a mean of 1.2 of 9 points, which the authors read as a sign the rubric may not be reliable](claims/engineering-rubric-low-scoring-reliability.md) [-W]; [Grade cutoffs are arbitrary because adjacent scores receiving different grades are not significantly different, per the author's statistical argument](claims/grade-cutoffs-arbitrary-adjacent-scores.md) [~W] (an argument)
rows.change: Several tasks or occasions; criteria and cut set in advance; two calibrated scorers on every judged task; review all scripts within a few marks of the cut; a reassessment route
rows.if: Stakes are high (certification, progression, licensing)

rows.basis: [Math anxiety has a small-to-moderate negative correlation with math achievement (r = −.28) in a meta-analysis of correlations from 223 studies](claims/math-anxiety-degrades-performance.md) [~M] (correlational); [Expressive Writing Improves Exam Performance](claims/expressive-writing-improves-exam-performance.md) [~M] (helped highly anxious ninth-graders in one study; a meta-analysis found a negligible effect); [Retrieval practice benefits learners regardless of trait anxiety level, but higher trait or induced anxiety is associated with smaller testing effects](claims/higher-anxiety-is-associated-with-smaller-testing-effects.md) [~M]
rows.change: Low-stakes quizzing through the course; untimed or generously timed papers where speed is not the outcome; weight spread over several occasions. A brief writing exercise about worries just before the exam is optional: evidence for it is mixed
rows.if: Learners have test anxiety, low confidence, or a history of failing exams

rows.basis: untested proposal; the measurement case is in [Validity, Reliability and Bias in Classroom Assessment](principles/validity-reliability-and-bias-in-classroom-assessment.md)
rows.change: Keep the language of items below the level being assessed; offer an oral or demonstrated response where the outcome is not reading or writing; gloss terms that are not the target
rows.if: Learners have low literacy, or are assessed in a second language

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give remote and in-room learners the same tasks, time and permitted aids; prefer open-book items that ask for application to a new case over recall that can be looked up; follow a sample of submissions with a short oral check of the learner's own work; make tasks readable on a phone screen
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, phone-only, or some learners remote while others sit in the room

rows.basis: [An adaptive mastery testing strategy reduces test length by 30% to 81% while reaching the same mastery decision as the conventional test for 96% of trainees](claims/adaptive-mastery-testing-reduces-length-preserves-decisions.md) [+W] (a military-training simulation); the marking plan is untested
rows.change: Machine-score the knowledge items; judge a smaller set of performance tasks with a short rubric; double-mark a sample of about one in ten, not all; return results by outcome with one comment each. A computerised adaptive test can shorten a mastery test while reaching nearly the same decision
rows.if: One teacher marks for a large group, or marking time is scarce (volunteers, a busy shift, one tutor)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do not report a summative judgment of the capability; give an end-of-session check, report it as immediate performance, and say what it cannot show
rows.if: Time is a single session only (a one-day workshop)

rows.basis: untested proposal; the task design is in [Authentic Assessment](patterns/authentic-assessment.md)
rows.change: Judge against the published criteria by trained assessors; record audience response as separate information, not as the grade; keep a component check for each criterion
rows.if: The end-point is a product or performance for a real audience (an exhibition, a client report, a recital)

rows.basis: [Dental students in a revised low-stress TBL format scored higher on the individual summative assessment (iSAT) than medical students in the original high-stakes format, in a non-randomised comparison of two cohorts](claims/low-stress-tbl-higher-isat-scores.md) [+W] (two cohorts, confounded); [Competitive (norm-referenced) grading pits students against one another and discourages cooperation, according to the author's argument](claims/competitive-grading-pits-students-against-each-other.md) [-W] (an argument)
rows.change: Keep an individual component in the summative grade; avoid grading on a curve, which sets team members against one another; consider lowering the stakes of in-module team tests
rows.if: Learners work in teams (team-based learning, group projects)

rows.basis: untested proposal; the three changes rest on the claims cited in the rows above
rows.change: Keep it. Change only what the evidence here speaks to: check its items against the outcomes and levels (one blueprint pass), add low-stakes retrieval before it, and calibrate scorers on a sample
rows.if: The brief names its own end-point (its own exam, rubric, grading scheme or portfolio)

rows.basis: the [whole-task claim](claims/whole-task-performance-improves-transfer.md) [~W] is a design argument; the rest is untested
rows.change: Keep a single whole-task scenario as the judgment; do not split it into paper items. Put recall and recognition checks into the low-stakes practice before it; inside the scenario, prompt the learner to say decisions aloud from the start and tell them the assessor will not confirm answers, so "is that what you wanted?" gets no reply and is not marked down
rows.if: The capability is one integrated performance (a clinical scenario, a full repair, a live service) and the brief asks for an authentic assessment

rows.basis: untested proposal; the earlier page's example of the advanced kindergarten reader who stops progressing
rows.change: Compact by pre-check within the class; give harder texts or problems in the same topic for the freed time; keep the student in class routines; review the arrangement every unit
rows.if: The student is a `child` in primary school, well ahead in reading or number

rows.basis: untested proposal; the earlier page's constraint that repeated grade-skipping opens large maturity gaps
rows.change: Subject acceleration in that subject (the next course, online or with an older class), with the student staying with their year group for other subjects
rows.if: The student is an `adolescent` in secondary school, ahead in one subject

rows.basis: untested proposal; the earlier page records that acceleration works but not indefinitely, citing a chapter not held as a claim
rows.change: Decide with the student, family and next teacher, on the student's work across subjects and their social readiness, for one grade at a time; set a review after the first term
rows.if: Whole-grade acceleration (grade-skipping) is being considered

rows.basis: [Adaptive learning improves outcomes](claims/adaptive-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+M] (general populations, not gifted students); [expertise reversal](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [+M] carried from training studies
rows.change: Prefer acceleration: move to the next unit's content once the pre-check is passed, through adaptive or self-paced material with a teacher check each week
rows.if: The target is cumulative (`procedure`, `principle`, as in mathematics or a language's grammar)

rows.basis: untested proposal; long expert development is described in [Even the most talented performers need around 10 years of intense involvement](claims/ten-year-rule-expert-performance.md) [~W] (a review, chess, music, sport)
rows.change: Prefer enrichment: an open task with a professional's standard and a real audience, with a mentor in the field where one can be found
rows.if: The target opens outwards (`complex-skill`, writing, art, music, a research project)

rows.basis: [Accumulated deliberate practice distinguishes more from less accomplished musicians](claims/deliberate-practice-hours-differentiate-musicians.md) [~W] (a review reporting one retrospective study); untested as a school design
rows.change: Count it: give access to training, a teacher or coach in the field, and practice time, and judge it by performance, not by an IQ score
rows.if: The talent is in music, art, sport or another field outside the academic subjects

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use one pre-check and two or three tiers of replacement work the teacher can run at once; check in with the ahead group together for 5 minutes twice a week rather than individually
rows.if: One teacher, a full mixed class, several students ahead at different points

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give the visiting adult one job each visit: read the latest draft, ask one question that raises the standard, and agree the next step and date; the contract carries the rest between visits
rows.if: Scarce teacher time (a busy class, a gifted coordinator who visits weekly, volunteer mentors)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Put the compacted student's replacement work and contract online; hold the weekly check-in as a short call; keep the student's role in the class's shared discussion when present
rows.if: Some students join remotely, or work from a phone or tablet at home

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give one hard, open task with a model of the standard, time to attempt it, and feedback naming what the student did; do not claim it as provision
rows.if: Only a single session is available (a one-off enrichment day, a visiting class)

rows.basis: [Extracurricular involvement and adult mentorship are associated with reversal of gifted underachievement](claims/extracurriculars-mentoring-reverse-underachievement.md) [+W] (one issue brief, associational)
rows.change: Check the work's level first (a pre-check on the next unit); if it is below the student's level, change the work before treating the behaviour; offer a mentor or an extracurricular in the area of talent
rows.if: The student is bored, handing in little or behaving badly

rows.basis: [Praise for intelligence rather than effort](claims/feedback-praise-reduces-learning.md) [+M] (fifth graders, general population; not gifted students)
rows.change: Set work hard enough that mistakes happen; name the student's strategy and effort, never "you're so smart"; show the student the improvement over drafts
rows.if: The student has low confidence, avoids hard work, or fears being wrong

rows.basis: [Underrepresentation of culturally and linguistically diverse students](claims/gifted-underrepresentation-diverse-students.md) [~W], [teacher under-referral](claims/teacher-underreferral-diverse-gifted.md) [~W] (one issue brief); [a talent search admitting by SAT score invited over 2,500 boys and 1,081 girls in one summer](claims/test-scores-gate-gifted-program-entry.md) [~W] (one witness's testimony); see [Standardized Test Fairness and Bias](principles/standardized-test-fairness-and-bias.md)
rows.change: Screen every student, use the unit pre-check as a second route in, and compare provision with enrolment by group each year
rows.if: Identification is by a test score cut-off, or by teacher referral

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep it. Change only what the evidence and the earlier page say matters: a pre-check on the unit's own work before deciding, replacement work that is harder rather than more, feedback that names what the student did, and the student's own interests in choosing the task
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (a school's gifted programme model, an extension menu, a published enrichment curriculum, its own rubric for advanced work)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use them, and raise the level by the task, not by substituting another rubric
rows.if: The brief's own rubric or criteria for the advanced work

rows.basis: [expertise reversal](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [+M] (electrical trainees, among others); untested as a test-out design
rows.change: Let them test out of modules by doing the module's task to its standard; give them the hardest cases or a role reviewing others' work for the freed time
rows.if: Adults in a work setting who are far ahead of a training course (an experienced hire in onboarding)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Plan the extension work towards it from the start, with the audience's standard as the criterion and at least one rehearsal or review by someone from that field
rows.if: The product is for a real audience (a competition, an exhibition, a published piece, a presentation to experts)

rows.basis: [Standardized Test Fairness and Bias](principles/standardized-test-fairness-and-bias.md) for score-based decisions; [Traditional gifted identification tests cannot fully determine learning potential](claims/traditional-identification-tests-fail-learning-potential.md) [~W] (an argument in one review)
rows.change: Decide on more than one source of evidence (the student's work across units, a pre-check on the next level, the student's own view), never a single score; record the decision and review it after one term
rows.if: Stakes are high (programme entry, a grade-skip, an accelerated exam entry)

rows.basis: [Praise for intelligence rather than effort](claims/feedback-praise-reduces-learning.md) [+M] (fifth graders, general population) for the feedback; the rest untested
rows.change: Keep steps short (5–10 minutes of focused practice), practise daily inside routines, name what the student did after each success, and use pictures or objects for each step
rows.if: The student is a `child` in primary school

rows.basis: [Self-determination instruction](claims/self-determination-instruction-improves-outcomes.md) [+M] and [student-led IEP meetings](claims/self-directed-iep-increases-student-participation.md) [+M] (high-school students with intellectual or learning disabilities); post-school outcomes not measured
rows.change: Move practice into community and workplace tasks; teach the student to set and review their own goals weekly and to lead their own planning meeting, rehearsed beforehand
rows.if: The student is an `adolescent` or young `adult` near transition (work, independent living)

rows.basis: [Mnemonic instruction](claims/mnemonic-instruction-improves-recall-for-students-with-disabilities.md) [+M] (includes mild developmental disabilities; recall outcomes, abstracts)
rows.change: Add a keyword or acrostic cue the student can decode, practise retrieving through it, and review it at spaced intervals
rows.if: The target is facts or vocabulary (`verbal-association`)

rows.basis: untested; the mnemonic claim's own page says benefits shrink for conceptual content
rows.change: Do not rely on mnemonics; teach with concrete objects and the real setting, and check with a changed task the memorised steps would not solve
rows.if: The target is understanding a `principle` or using a skill in a new setting

rows.basis: untested proposal; mastery pacing ([Mastery learning improves outcomes](claims/mastery-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [+M]) carried from general classes
rows.change: Teach it as a task analysis of 4–8 steps in its real setting, practise until three consecutive unaided successes on two days, then fade to weekly review
rows.if: The target is a daily-life `procedure` (money, time, travel)

rows.basis: [Peer tutoring improves achievement](claims/peer-tutoring-improves-achievement.md) [+M] (tutee ability level not a moderator, mathematics); the rest untested
rows.change: Build the student's steps into the class task (same activity, smaller step, picture checklist), seat a trained peer partner, and check the student's attempt first when circulating
rows.if: One teacher, a full general class, the student needs intermittent support

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give the visiting adult one job: watch one attempt at the current step, record which step was reached, and set the next step; leave a picture checklist so the student and a peer can practise in between
rows.if: Scarce adult time (a shared aide, a specialist who visits weekly, volunteers)

rows.basis: untested proposal; [parent-delivered intervention](claims/parent-implemented-intervention-improves-outcomes.md) [+M] is evidence for children with autism only
rows.change: Send the same step and checklist home with a short video model of the step; have the student or a family member show one attempt on video or in a call each week; keep the in-class group role when the student is present
rows.if: Some learners join remotely, or the student works from a phone or tablet at home

rows.basis: [Aided AAC systems over manual signs](claims/aided-systems-advantage-over-manual-signs.md) [+W] (a review's report, children with autism, a tendency); for the planning move see [Universal Design for Learning](principles/universal-design-for-learning.md)
rows.change: Give a way to respond that does not depend on speech or print (pointing, a picture or symbol board, a speech-generating device), and keep the same academic target
rows.if: The student has limited speech or does not read yet

rows.basis: [Praise for intelligence rather than effort](claims/feedback-praise-reduces-learning.md) [+M] (children after failure, general population); choice untested here
rows.change: Restart one step below where they failed so that the first attempts succeed, name each success specifically, and let the student choose which of two practice tasks to do first
rows.if: The student has low confidence after repeated failure, or avoids tasks

rows.basis: [Self-monitoring improves on-task behavior](claims/self-monitoring-improves-on-task-behavior.md) [+M] (single-case studies, students with or at risk for disabilities; on-task behaviour, not achievement)
rows.change: Teach the student to check and record at intervals whether they are working (a cue every few minutes, a tally card or app), alongside the step checklist
rows.if: The student has trouble staying with a task during independent practice

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Teach one step of one functional task, practise it three or four times with feedback naming what the student did, and end with one unaided attempt; record what it shows and do not claim retention
rows.if: Only a single session is available (a one-off workshop, a visiting class)

rows.basis: untested proposal; from the earlier page's inclusion guidance
rows.change: Give the student a defined, rehearsed part with a visual script; rehearse in the real space at least twice; agree beforehand how they can ask for help during it
rows.if: The product is shown to a real audience (a class presentation, a school event, a job trial)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep it. Change only what the evidence says matters: one observable step per goal, feedback that names what the student did rather than the student, a practice dose the timetable actually holds, and the student stating the goal themselves
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (an IEP goal format, a school's praise or reward system, a published curriculum, a specialist's prompt hierarchy)

rows.basis: [Teacher expectation effects](claims/teacher-expectation-effects-on-achievement.md) [~M] (associational, general cohort); the rest untested
rows.change: Judge readiness on unaided attempts in the real setting, never on assisted success; record every prompt given; check the target is still the age-appropriate one, not one lowered to fit the label
rows.if: Stakes are high (a placement decision, an accountability test, a work trial)

rows.basis: [The Self-Determined Learning Model of Instruction improves self-determination](claims/self-determined-learning-model-of-instruction-improves-self-determination.md) [~M] (312 high-school students; within-group gains, small non-significant difference from controls)
rows.change: Keep the student answering the model's questions and train the adult to facilitate, not answer for them; do not expect a gain over usual instruction to be shown
rows.if: The plan is the student's choice of goals (self-determined learning model)

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page ("some learners comprehend better through print")
rows.change: Do not build the lesson around speech; offer it as an optional control for fatigue or proofreading only, and keep it off during reading practice and any check of reading
rows.if: Learners are fluent readers of this text (`advanced` for its print), or the goal includes reading the words unaided

rows.basis: [Repeated listening improves oral reading fluency in second-grade students, with Listening Only outgaining Reading While Listening and Reading Only](claims/repeated-listening-improves-oral-reading-fluency.md) [~M] (one seven-week study of 75 second graders, reported second-hand in a review; reading while listening had the smallest fluency gain and an average comprehension loss; no statistical test printed)
rows.change: Use speech or read-along for access to stories and content above their reading level, not as the main fluency practice; keep the child reading the words aloud themselves in separate practice, and check comprehension after read-along rather than assuming it
rows.if: Learners are `child` early readers building fluency

rows.basis: [Audio narration with finger-tracking animation directs bilingual preschoolers' attention to the target-language print in dual-language e-books, including the nondominant language](claims/enhancing-features-direct-attention-dual-language-e-books.md) [+M]; [Multimedia features improved story comprehension in dual-language e-books (marginal trend) but not in single-language e-books](claims/comprehension-benefit-dual-language-only.md) [~M] (one eye-tracking study, bilingual preschoolers)
rows.change: Choose narration with a highlight that tracks the words, in the language whose print the child should look at; ask two or three story questions after, since attention to print did not reliably become comprehension
rows.if: Young children with an e-book or app, possibly in two languages

rows.basis: [Phonics instruction has a small but statistically confirmed effect for children with reading disabilities, while Orton-Gillingham structured-literacy programs show positive but non-significant effects](claims/structured-literacy-interventions-help-struggling-readers.md) [~M] (speech itself untested here)
rows.change: Give speech for content reading and tests of content in every subject; keep explicit decoding instruction in its own time; record that the content scores were earned with speech
rows.if: Learners have a reading disability or dyslexia

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page (vision loss); [Universal Design for Learning](principles/universal-design-for-learning.md) holds the alternative-route rule
rows.change: The learner will not follow print, so make the text navigable by ear: real headings, alternative text on images, tables that read in order, equations in a speakable form; let the learner use their own screen reader and settings rather than an in-app voice
rows.if: Learners have low vision or are blind and use a screen reader

rows.basis: [Reading and listening yield similar proportions of incidental vocabulary learning, with reading ahead only on some immediate posttests](claims/reading-versus-listening-incidental-vocabulary-gains.md) [~S] (second-language vocabulary only; says nothing about synthetic voices)
rows.change: Use speech to hear the pronunciation of new words while reading them and to read along with texts at their listening level; expect vocabulary from listening or read-along to be learned at proportions similar to reading, with reading ahead on immediate tests only
rows.if: Second-language learners

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Let workers listen to the document on their own device, in sections, and act on each section (find the step, fill the field) rather than only listen; fix the voice's pronunciation of product names and codes first
rows.if: Adults in work settings (manuals, procedures, compliance documents, forms)

rows.basis: [Presenting words as spoken narration rather than on-screen text alongside graphics improves learning](claims/modality-effect-narration-over-text.md) [~S]; [Redundant on-screen text impairs learning when it competes with a visualization, though written text duplicating narration alone can help](claims/redundancy-principle.md) [~M] (multimedia lessons with recorded narration, carried to synthetic speech)
rows.change: Speak the explanation and show only labels and key terms on the visual; if the learner controls pace, full text can stay available on demand
rows.if: The text explains a diagram, animation or chart

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page (synthetic voices distort domain vocabulary)
rows.change: Do not rely on default speech; provide a version written for listening or a human recording, or limit speech to the prose around the notation
rows.if: Text is dense with notation (equations, code, tables, citations)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Build the speech control into every page and question, put a question or summary prompt at each section break with automatic checking where possible, and add the periodic with/without check from the default arc
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give everyone the same digital text so each can use their own device's speech with headphones; for phone-only learners, keep sections short enough for one screen and avoid layouts that read out of order
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners remote, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Make speech available to all rather than assigned to a few; at each section break use a whole-class check (a quick poll or one written line) so the teacher sees who is lost, and go to those learners
rows.if: One teacher for a large class

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Spend the facilitator's time once, on showing the controls and the section-break routine; after that, the learner works alone with the supplied questions, and the facilitator looks only at the answers to one or two questions per text
rows.if: Scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, a brief check-in)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Ten minutes on the controls with a short text, then one section-by-section reading of the real text with supplied questions; record the answers and do not claim lasting benefit
rows.if: A single session only

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Offer speech privately (headphones, own device), as a normal option for everyone rather than a label; let the learner choose rate and voice; start on short texts that matter to them
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or low literacy, adult or child

rows.basis: untested; follows from step 1
rows.change: If the test measures content, allow speech as an accommodation and say so in the record; if it measures reading, do not, and give the learner a fair version of the test that does not depend on speech for its instructions
rows.if: Stakes are high, or the test is meant to measure reading

rows.basis: untested proposal (a lesson from page testing, not from a claim)
rows.change: Keep that routine and its categories as given; add only speech for the text and a break at each section where the routine's own question or code is applied
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (its reading log, question set, rubric, annotation code or listening guide)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: The learner decides who hears it: headphones, their own device, and an on-device voice rather than a cloud service where the text would leave the device; nobody else listens unless the learner asks
rows.if: The material is private or sensitive (a learner's own writing, a health or HR document, a personal letter)

rows.basis: untested proposal (speech runs at roughly the voice's set rate, so time the actual audio first)
rows.change: Fit the text to it: one text of about 600–900 words in three or four sections, 3–4 minutes of listening per section plus one minute at each break, the last five minutes for the brief's own task
rows.if: A fixed short time budget (for example, 20 minutes)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the real document and the real decision; use speech and section breaks inside it, and do not split it into separate comprehension items
rows.if: The brief wants a whole task kept whole (read a real policy and decide; follow a real procedure)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: For proofreading, have the learner listen to their draft at a slow rate and mark every place it sounds wrong. For audio a real audience will hear, check every name and term by ear and have a person approve it before release
rows.if: Learners use speech on their own writing, or produce audio for a real audience (an announcement, a podcast, a museum guide)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use short texts (about 100–250 words, one procedure) read sentence by sentence; teach playback control as a skill (slow the voice, replay a sentence, replay a single word for pronunciation) and let learners practise privately with headphones; give teacher feedback in a form TTS can read aloud; each lesson end with one unaided reread of a step. If the brief names its own assessment (accuracy, control of playback, a reflection comparing listening and unaided reading), assess exactly those, and keep checks to one or two items so the class is not mostly testing
rows.if: Adult second-language learners in short evening classes, reading workplace instructions

rows.basis: [Part-task practice reduces cognitive load for absolute novices during initial skill acquisition.](claims/part-task-practice-reduces-load-for-novices.md) [~M] (load, not transfer); [interleaving](claims/interleaving-improves-inductive-learning.md) [~M] (claim page notes novel material can reverse the benefit)
rows.change: Secure the taught case first with worked examples and guided practice; start with two cases, not four; practise parts briefly before integrating; delay mixing until each type has been introduced
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on this task, or the task is high in element interactivity

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (review of cognitive-load studies; not about transfer designs)
rows.change: Skip the early stage; give unprompted varied and far cases with selective feedback, and ask learners to generate their own cases
rows.if: Learners are `advanced`, or already solve the taught case unaided

rows.basis: untested; the case-comparison and retrieval-transfer evidence here is mostly with undergraduates
rows.change: Use concrete, familiar surface forms; give the comparison prompt every time and state the principle yourself; keep to two cases per session
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: [The closer training content is to authentic clinical scenarios, the smoother its translation into practice](claims/contextualized-teaching-facilitates-transfer.md) [+W] (interviews with neurosurgical nurses; perceived, not measured)
rows.change: Take the late-stage cases from their own work; ask them to bring one; check that their workplace offers the cases and equipment to use the skill
rows.if: Learners are `adult` or professionals

rows.basis: [Analogical Reasoning Improves Transfer](claims/analogical-reasoning-improves-transfer.md) [+S] (undergraduates, negotiation; meta-analysis across domains)
rows.change: Pair cases and prompt comparison before stating the principle; test on new cases rather than definitions
rows.if: Goal is a `principle` or `concept` to be used in new cases

rows.basis: [Interleaving category examples improves inductive category learning for visual and mathematical materials, but not for expository texts or word categories](claims/interleaving-improves-inductive-learning.md) [~M] (classification of new examples; smaller for mathematics, reversed for word categories)
rows.change: Mix problem types in practice once each is introduced, so the learner must decide which applies; expect slower, error-prone practice
rows.if: Goal is choosing among several `procedure`s (which method fits which problem)

rows.basis: [Task rehearsal improves fluency and complexity on the repeated task but does not transfer to a new task of the same type](claims/task-repetition-fluency-complexity-same-task-only.md) [~M] (second-hand report of one language-learning study)
rows.change: Vary the task within the type rather than repeating one task; repeat a task only to build fluency on that task
rows.if: Goal is spoken or performed fluency on a type of task (e.g. a language task)

rows.basis: [Retrieval Practice Improves Transfer](claims/retrieval-practice-improves-transfer.md) [~S] (lab and prose-passage studies; carried to self-paced courses untested)
rows.change: Build the comparison prompt and the principle statement into the materials; use automatically checked retrieval questions in changed formats; add an unprompted transfer item before the next unit
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: [Analogical Reasoning Improves Transfer](claims/analogical-reasoning-improves-transfer.md) [+S] (immediate tests favoured in the meta-analysis)
rows.change: Teach two cases side by side, prompt the comparison, state the principle, and end with one near-transfer item; do not claim far or delayed transfer
rows.if: Time is one session only

rows.basis: untested; the comparison evidence includes classroom experiments in the meta-analysis but no class-size result
rows.change: Pairs compare the two cases on one sheet and write what is the same; the teacher collects answers and states the principle from them; every learner does one unaided transfer item on paper
rows.if: `classroom` with one teacher and a large group

rows.basis: [All learners … showed a floor effect on far-transfer problems](claims/far-transfer-floor-effect-and-equal-time.md) [~M]; [no increases for far-transfer problems](claims/germane-load-gains-limited-to-identical-and-near-transfer-problems.md) [~W] (one study each, engineering and a game task)
rows.change: Add cases from the target domain itself rather than relying on transfer from another; assess on representative target tasks after a delay
rows.if: Stakes are high, or the objective is far transfer to another domain

rows.basis: [Transfer of advanced competencies is limited by institutional case exposure, technical platforms, and multidisciplinary maturity rather than training deficiencies](claims/advanced-competency-transfer-limited-by-institutional-resources.md) [~W] (interviews, one programme in China)
rows.change: Agree with the workplace when the learner will meet the cases; plan refresher cases or simulation if they will not; report use separately from knowledge
rows.if: `workplace-clinical`, and the course teaches advanced competencies the setting rarely uses

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] and [Multiple representations improve learning](claims/multiple-representations-improve-learning.md) [~M] (benefit depends on skill at connecting representations); bounding the number of options is untested
rows.change: Curate options to two or three; integrate representations rather than offering many in parallel; model each choice before asking for it
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on this content

rows.basis: [Instructional guidance that helps novices can become redundant or counterproductive as expertise grows.](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (cognitive-load studies; no crossover point given)
rows.change: Drop the extra representations and step-by-step supports by default and leave them available on request; widen choice of task and format
rows.if: Learners are `advanced`, or succeed on the first task unaided

rows.basis: untested proposal; the learning-styles experiment with fifth graders shows only that matching to a reported style did not help ([Learning Styles Matching Does Not Improve Learning](claims/learning-styles-matching-does-not-improve-learning.md) [~S])
rows.change: Fewer, concrete choices (pick one of two); the teacher demonstrates each support; read-aloud and picture supports by default
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: [modifications may be necessary for older beginners and learners with disabilities](claims/modifications-essential-for-vulnerable-learners.md) [~W] (one practitioner's judgment, adult ESL)
rows.change: Ask learners which barriers they meet; keep individual accommodations; offer formats drawn from their own work
rows.if: Learners are `adult` or professionals, including older beginners or learners with disabilities

rows.basis: [Learning Styles Matching Does Not Improve Learning](claims/learning-styles-matching-does-not-improve-learning.md) [~S] (systematic review and a randomized experiment with fifth graders)
rows.change: Do not; offer the routes to everyone and let content decide the primary mode (a diagram for spatial structure, speech for pronunciation)
rows.if: A colleague proposes assigning materials by each learner's "learning style"

rows.basis: [Multiple representations improve learning](claims/multiple-representations-improve-learning.md) [+M] (undergraduate physics, one field study) and [Adding relevant pictures or graphics to text improves learning from it, with a small pooled effect on reading comprehension, though whether dual coding explains the benefit is disputed](claims/dual-coding-improves-learning.md) [+S] (comprehension from text with graphics)
rows.change: Pair a visual and a verbal representation of the same relation and ask learners to translate between them; feedback on the process, not only the answer
rows.if: Goal is a `concept` or `principle`

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page (options in how learners engage and access, not in what they are expected to learn)
rows.change: Keep the expression format fixed; vary only the routes into the content and the practice supports
rows.if: Goal is a `procedure` or `complex-skill` whose format *is* the goal (handwriting, oral fluency, a clinical technique)

rows.basis: [Letting learners pace instruction helped on complex material in one experiment](claims/learner-paced-beats-system-paced-complex-material.md) [~M] (primary-school animation and a meta-analysis of learner control; achievement gain not general); the rest untested
rows.change: Build the access layers into the media (editable text, captions and transcripts, pause and replay, glossary links); give automatic, criterion-referenced feedback on each product format
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: [Redundant on-screen text impairs learning when it competes with a visualization](claims/redundancy-principle.md) [~M] (lab multimedia lessons; captions remain a necessary accommodation for deaf and hard-of-hearing learners)
rows.change: Captions on request rather than always on; put essential words in the narration; give a transcript separately
rows.if: Narrated video or animation is the main medium

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Offer choice at the level of the whole task (two versions of one activity) rather than per learner; one shared rubric displayed for all formats; check-ins on who is stuck
rows.if: `classroom` with one teacher and a large group

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Do only steps 1, 3 and 4 (goal, two routes into the content, segmenting and pause); skip format choice
rows.if: Time is a single session

rows.basis: untested proposal; the concern that a single verbal format underestimates some learners is [an argument](claims/verbal-achievement-tests-may-underestimate-via-symbolic-mismatch.md) [+W]
rows.change: Validate that each expression format measures the same capability before allowing it; mark anchor samples in every format; record accommodations given
rows.if: Stakes are high (certification, grading)

rows.basis: [Autonomy support increases intrinsic motivation, engagement, and persistence](claims/autonomy-supports-intrinsic-motivation.md) [+M] (motivation outcomes; learning outcomes weaker, see [Autonomy](principles/autonomy.md))
rows.change: Add a stated reason for the work and one meaningful choice per session; replace controlling incentives and language with informational feedback
rows.if: Learners have stopped engaging, or work only for marks

rows.basis: [Raters differed in severity](claims/raters-differed-severity-mfrm.md) [~M] (open-ended items, three raters); [rubric guidance improved peer raters' placement of writing on complex criteria](claims/rubrics-improve-peer-feedback-quality.md) [+M] (MOOC and graduate peers, carried to teachers); one class's rubric scores varied by a mean of 1.2 of 9 points across six scorers ([engineering rubric low scoring reliability](claims/engineering-rubric-low-scoring-reliability.md) [~W])
rows.change: Use a performance task scored by a rubric with level descriptors and anchors; calibrate markers before marking and double-mark a sample; report the score with the number of tasks it rests on
rows.if: The goal is a `complex-skill` or extended performance (a lab, an essay, a presentation, a clinical task)

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page (item-count arithmetic, selected-response trade-off)
rows.change: Use many short selected-response or short-answer items for breadth and reliability; keep the language plain; add a few items that ask for the procedure on a changed case if transfer matters
rows.if: The goal is `verbal-association` or a `procedure` recalled or carried out quickly

rows.basis: [Verbal tests may underestimate subject knowledge](claims/verbal-achievement-tests-may-underestimate-via-symbolic-mismatch.md) [~W] (argument); the fractions example is from the earlier page (Linn & Miller)
rows.change: Keep reading load below the target; gloss non-target words; read items aloud or allow a spoken, drawn or demonstrated answer where reading is not the construct; do not read a low score as low content knowledge without a second, low-language check
rows.if: Learners are learning in a second language, or have low literacy

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use pictures, objects and spoken instructions; short sessions; observe the performance rather than relying on written answers; more occasions, fewer items per occasion
rows.if: Learners are young children (`child`)

rows.basis: [Male-oriented item content biases scores](claims/male-oriented-item-content-biases-test-scores.md) [~W] (second-hand); a Korean translation of a psychosocial measure kept acceptable reliability but its inter-scale correlations were not as expected in 79 immigrant adults ([cross-cultural measurement bias in translated instruments](claims/cross-cultural-measurement-bias-in-translated-psychosocial-instruments.md) [~W]; adults, research instrument, carried to classroom questionnaires)
rows.change: Review every context for taught or shared knowledge; balance people in items; for a translated self-report scale, check its internal consistency and whether its scales relate to each other as expected in your own group before interpreting scores
rows.if: Learners come from varied cultural or national backgrounds, or a questionnaire has been translated

rows.basis: [Math anxiety degrades performance](claims/math-anxiety-degrades-performance.md) [~M] (meta-analysis of correlations; does not test these moves)
rows.change: Drop time limits unless speed is the target; give low-stakes practice in the same format first; allow scratch work; interpret a score from a timed, high-pressure sitting with caution
rows.if: Learners are anxious about tests, or mathematics anxiety is common in the group

rows.basis: [Decision consistency lowest at the distribution peak](claims/dc-lowest-at-score-distribution-peak.md) [~M] (simulation); [Cohen's kappa paradox](claims/cohens-kappa-paradox-decision-consistency.md) [~W] (worked example); [grade cutoffs arbitrary](claims/grade-cutoffs-arbitrary-adjacent-scores.md) [~W] (argument)
rows.change: Put more items or tasks behind the decision; seek a second piece of evidence for learners near the cut; report decision consistency rather than kappa; allow a re-take or appeal on a comparable task
rows.if: Stakes are high: a grade boundary, pass mark, placement or certification

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page (a single item's weight in a short test)
rows.change: Use it to steer the next lesson, not to grade an individual; aim the few items at the one decision you need; combine with other evidence before any grade
rows.if: Time is one session only, or the assessment is a single short quiz

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use selected-response or short-answer items for breadth; reserve judgement-scored tasks for the objectives that need them; mark one question across all scripts at a time rather than one script at a time; re-mark the first ten scripts at the end to check for drift
rows.if: One teacher marks for a large group

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give every learner the same items, aids and time, or record the difference beside the score; avoid long passages, drag-and-drop and wide tables for phone users; compare remote and in-room score distributions before treating them as one set; for a performance, use the same observer checklist live and on video
rows.if: Learners take the assessment in mixed modes: some in the room, some remote, some on phones only

rows.basis: An interview rating of teachers' use of an innovation correlated .65 with readers' ratings of written ethnographic protocols, which its authors read as support for its validity ([LoU interview validated against observation](claims/lou-interview-validated-against-ethnography.md) [+W]; teachers, research instrument; the way validity was checked is carried, not a result about learners)
rows.change: Assess the task as it is done at work, with an observer checklist; use two observers on a sample; check validity by comparing the assessment's ratings with independent observation of practice
rows.if: Adults in work settings, or the capability is a job task

rows.basis: untested proposal; the audience relationship is owned by [Authentic Audiences and Purposes](principles/authentic-audiences-purposes.md)
rows.change: Score it against the criteria by markers who have calibrated, separately from the audience's reaction; record audience response as its own observation, not as the grade
rows.if: The work is a product or performance for a real audience

rows.basis: [Ignoring local dependence overestimates reliability](claims/ignored-local-dependence-overestimates-reliability-simulation.md) [~M] (simulation of a large-scale reading test)
rows.change: Count passages, not items, when judging whether there is enough evidence; estimate consistency at the passage level
rows.if: The test uses several items on one passage, case or data set

rows.basis: [Later-positioned item more difficult](claims/later-position-item-more-difficult-fatigue-effect.md) [~M] (national examination; one item)
rows.change: Keep item order fixed across versions, or compare an item's difficulty across positions before treating versions as equal
rows.if: Several versions of the test exist (shuffled order, A/B forms)

rows.basis: untested; the strategy page's view that the framing is redundant for confident learners with established trust
rows.change: Keep the critique and the named standard; shorten the assurance to one clause; do not drop the critique to protect the relationship
rows.if: The learner already trusts the giver, or has a long record of success with them

rows.basis: [Praise for intelligence, rather than for effort, after success undermines children's motivation and performance after a later failure](claims/feedback-praise-reduces-learning.md) [-M] (fifth graders; tests the praise, not the framing)
rows.change: Give the three parts spoken, short and about the work; praise the strategy or effort, never "smart"; the assurance in plain words ("I know you can get this part right; let's try it again now") and an immediate second attempt
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: untested here; the earlier page and the strategy page's account of field experiments with seventh graders, which have no claim page
rows.change: Put the standard-and-assurance sentence at the top of the written comments, before the critique, and require a revision
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent`, with written feedback on graded work

rows.basis: untested; [Feedback improves learning by a medium amount on average, but its effect varies widely with the information it carries, and more than a third of feedback interventions reduce performance](claims/feedback-improves-learning.md) [~S] covers field and work settings and warns that feedback turning attention to the self can lower performance
rows.change: Name the job's own standard (the competency, the protocol, the client outcome) as the standard; say what in the learner's practice shows they can meet it; agree one change to try on the next shift or case
rows.if: `adult` learners in `workplace-clinical` settings (a supervisor, mentor or clinical educator across a difference)

rows.basis: [Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~M], carried: brief belonging messages helped stereotyped groups at college entry, and only where the institution gave them opportunities to belong; it does not test feedback
rows.change: Use the same three parts; time the first framed critique for the transition point (first assignment of the course or programme)
rows.if: The difference is a stereotype in the domain rather than between teacher and learner (women in engineering, first-generation students, adults returning to study)

rows.basis: untested proposal (wave 6 lesson)
rows.change: Use them as "the standard" in the framing sentence and the critique; do not substitute this page's or another rubric
rows.if: The brief names its own rubric, criteria or categories

rows.basis: untested proposal (wave 5 lesson)
rows.change: Keep it; add only the standard-and-assurance sentence and a revision date, and check the "grow" part names a next step
rows.if: The brief names its own feedback routine (glow-and-grow, a comment template, a conference script)

rows.basis: untested proposal; a template with no personal clause is expected to read as generic
rows.change: Write one framing sentence once and reuse it, but add one clause that names something in this learner's work; cap the critique at two points; a fixed time budget of about 2–3 minutes per piece: 30 seconds for the framing, 1–2 minutes for two critiques with next steps, 30 seconds for the revision date
rows.if: One teacher for many learners, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, a tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: untested; carried from the belonging message's "common and passing" framing ([Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~M])
rows.change: A system cannot credibly state personal belief; state the standard, the specific gap and the next step, and say that learners at this point commonly reach the standard on revision (only if your data show it); route learners who stall to a person
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, automated feedback, no instructor present

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give critical feedback privately, in writing or one-to-one, never in front of the group or the camera; on a phone, put the standard and assurance in the first line and one next step in the second, with the full comments attached
rows.if: Mixed modes (some remote, some in the room) or phone-only learners

rows.basis: [A brief values-affirmation writing exercise raised African American seventh-graders' grades in two small field experiments, but a large same-district replication found no effect](claims/self-affirmation-improves-outcomes.md) [~M] and [Growth-mindset interventions have weak average effects on achievement, including a negligible GPA gain (d = 0.11) for lower-achieving US ninth-graders in one preregistered national trial](claims/growth-mindset-improves-achievement.md) [~M]: one-off identity-targeted messages are fragile
rows.change: Consistency cannot build; make the assurance concrete by pointing to evidence in the work, and give one revision in the session; claim no lasting effect
rows.if: A single session only (one workshop, one assessed piece, a one-off review)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Give the framed critique on a draft before the summative submission; keep the grade and its justification separate from the developmental comments
rows.if: High stakes (a summative grade, certification, a placement decision)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Speak the three parts, or write them in plain language; one critique at a time; ask the learner to say back the next step before they start
rows.if: Learners with low confidence, low literacy, or working in a second language

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: The learner controls who sees the work and the feedback; comment only to the learner; ask before mentioning it to parents or colleagues
rows.if: Private or sensitive work (personal writing, identity, a disclosure)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Hold the critique to the audience's standard, on the whole product, before release; the assurance is that the learner can get it ready for that audience
rows.if: A product or performance for a real audience, which the brief wants kept whole

rows.basis: untested; the earlier page. [Parent Involvement Improves Achievement](claims/parent-involvement-improves-achievement.md) [+W], carried: parents' high expectations and communication about school go with achievement (correlational)
rows.change: Specific positive, the concern with evidence, the standard and your belief in the student, one thing to support at home; offer an interpreter where needed
rows.if: A conversation with parents or guardians

rows.basis: [Brief Intervention Empathic Discipline Cuts Suspensions](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [~M] (a teacher-side exercise narrowed a racial disparity in suspensions; small overall effect in the preregistered replication) and [Belonging Interventions Improve Outcomes](claims/belonging-interventions-improve-outcomes.md) [~M] (effect only where the context afforded belonging)
rows.change: Raise it as a design constraint: the framing alone will not hold; pair it with changes on the teacher side
rows.if: The institution's grading, discipline or placement practice contradicts the message

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Design it as practice for the feedback-giver: model one annotated example, have them rewrite a real critique in the three-part form (criterion, high standard, assurance plus a specific next step) against the brief's own rubric, rehearse it in role-play with a peer playing the learner, and review recordings or notes against a short checklist before the real assessment
rows.if: The learner is the person who gives the feedback (a tutor, mentor or assessor being trained)

rows.basis: [Guided rather than unassisted discovery](claims/guided-discovery-outperforms-pure-discovery.md) [~S]; its studies did not use authentic assessment tasks, and the meta-analysis does not break results down by prior knowledge
rows.change: Spend the first half of the unit on component practice with worked examples; use a simpler, well-structured version of the task for the first draft; plan two revision cycles; give feedback on each component before the whole task.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain (first course, first placement)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Drop most component practice; give an ill-structured task in which learners define part of the problem; one draft with practitioner feedback; judge by a practitioner panel.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or practitioners (final-year students, continuing professional education)

rows.basis: [Authentic audiences](claims/authentic-audiences-improve-student-work.md) [+M]: second-graders wrote better for an external audience (one study, abstract only); the rest is untested
rows.change: Keep the task short and concrete with one product, one audience the children know of (another class, families), criteria as two or three "I can" statements, and teacher-led feedback rather than peer scoring.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary school)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's direct-instruction qualification
rows.change: Assess it with a conventional test or a short structured task; keep the authentic task for the capability that needs it, or use it as a capstone after the procedures are secure.
rows.if: The goal is a well-defined procedure or factual knowledge

rows.basis: [Trainees' reports on clinical scenarios](claims/contextualized-teaching-facilitates-transfer.md) [+W] (one qualitative study of neurosurgical nurses); [simulated cases judged unrealistic](claims/simucase-lacks-behavioral-authenticity.md) [~W] (10 graduate students, focus groups)
rows.change: Use structured clinical or practical stations with checklists and global ratings, or a case simulation, and check with learners whether the simulated case behaves like real clients.
rows.if: `workplace-clinical` or a placement-based course

rows.basis: [Peer assessment](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M] (robust to online or offline delivery in the meta-analysis); [self-assessment training](claims/self-assessment-accuracy-is-low-without-training.md) [~S]; carried to authentic tasks untested
rows.change: Give the rubric and scored exemplars up front; have learners score an exemplar and see the expert's score before self-assessing; use structured peer review in a timed window; reserve teacher or practitioner judgement for the final product.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: [Peer assessment](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M]; [structured criteria not shown to beat freeform peer review](claims/peer-assessment-structured-criteria-improve-learning.md) [~M], so do not expect the rubric alone to lift the peer effect
rows.change: Use peer assessment with the rubric for the draft; teacher feedback on a sample plus whole-class feedback on common problems; double-score only a sample of finals and products near the threshold.
rows.if: Large class (more than about 60) or little assessor time

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Shrink the task to one realistic decision or product, give one feedback point before submission, and drop the public exhibition.
rows.if: Short time (one or two weeks, or a single session)

rows.basis: [Rubric scores spread across scorers](claims/engineering-rubric-low-scoring-reliability.md) [~W] (one class, six teams); the remedy is untested
rows.change: Use at least two tasks or stations, calibrate assessors on exemplars and check agreement before scores are released, set the threshold in advance, and keep a reassessment route.
rows.if: High stakes (grade, progression or licensure)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page. [The rubric study with pre-service teachers](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [~M] found more stress and performance-avoidance with rubric use
rows.change: Rehearse privately with feedback first; make the first audience small and supportive; grade growth against criteria, not comparison with peers.
rows.if: Learners anxious or new to public performance

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Let learners choose the context or product form where the target allows; give the rubric in plain language; score the target reasoning apart from language mechanics; allow oral or multimodal products.
rows.if: Mixed language backgrounds or unequal access to resources

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Include a live or observed part (an oral defence, a supervised station, a recorded process) and ask learners to explain decisions in the product.
rows.if: Learners use AI tools freely outside class

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Split the submission: the product as the audience would receive it, scored on audience criteria (relevance, clarity, usability), plus a short decision memo for the assessor (sources checked, priorities weighed, what is uncertain and how the product handles it), scored on the reasoning criteria; give feedback and the revision on both
rows.if: The real product goes to a client or audience who should not see the working (an advice letter, a patient leaflet, a pitch)
