rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Keep each online exposition segment short, with an embedded check and worked material, and spend the in-person time on guided practice with feedback before independent work.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the content

rows.basis: untested proposal; the recorded synthesis is mostly higher education and professional training
rows.change: Run the online part in school time under supervision (rotation between stations or groups) rather than at home, and keep online segments short; give the teacher a view of who completed what.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (`pre-k-12`)

rows.basis: [Blended learning improves outcomes](claims/blended-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [~M], pooled mostly across higher education and professional training, with extra time and resources confounded
rows.change: Put content and repeated practice online where they can fit it around work; use in-person time for practice with equipment, cases or colleagues and for feedback on performance.
rows.if: Learners are `adult` working professionals (`adult-workplace`)

rows.basis: [Active learning improves exam performance](claims/active-learning-improves-exam-performance.md) [+M], tested against lecture in undergraduate STEM courses, not within a blend
rows.change: Reserve most in-person time for learners carrying out the task with feedback, not for exposition; move the exposition online.
rows.if: The goal is a `complex-skill` or `procedure` that needs practice with feedback

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Put spaced, self-checked practice online with immediate answers; keep in-person time for using the material and for checks of what was missed.
rows.if: The goal is mostly facts or vocabulary (`verbal-association`)

rows.basis: [SRL interventions in online and blended environments](claims/srl-interventions-moderate-effect-online-blended.md) [+M], pooled across 15 studies, populations not reported on the claim page
rows.change: Add planning prompts, a visible schedule with intermediate deadlines and self-monitoring checks; review them at the next in-person session.
rows.if: The online part is `online-self-paced` and learners have little experience of it

rows.basis: [Online continuing-education persistence](claims/online-continuing-education-persistence-lower-than-onground.md) [~W], fully online adult continuing education, associational; untested for blends
rows.change: Monitor completion each week, contact non-starters within the first week or two, and keep a named person learners can ask.
rows.if: No teacher present between sessions, or a large group

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Use a single online preparation task before the session and a short online follow-up; the course-level split does not apply.
rows.if: Only one session, or a few days

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Hold the summative assessment in person or proctored; keep the online checks low-stakes and formative so learners use them to monitor.
rows.if: High-stakes assessment

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Make the online part downloadable and usable on a phone, provide access time on site, and avoid live online slots that need a stable connection.
rows.if: Learners have limited devices or connectivity

rows.basis: [Prior knowledge and self-assessment](claims/prior-knowledge-needed-for-accurate-self-assessment.md) [~M] and [self-assessment accuracy](claims/self-assessment-accuracy-is-low-without-training.md) [~M], both about judging one's own performance, carried to judging others'
rows.change: Use anchor exemplars with known quality, three or four criteria with described levels, teacher modelling each session, and the reference comparison after every round; keep criteria to what learners can see in the object. Delay judging classmates' work until alone judgments of anchors are within a level.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain (cannot yet tell strong from weak work unaided)

rows.basis: [Rubric guidance](claims/rubrics-improve-peer-feedback-quality.md) [~M]: in a graduate course a rubric changed feedback content but restrained reflective and divergent commentary
rows.change: Have them co-construct criteria, judge genuinely borderline cases, and record reasoned disagreement instead of forcing consensus; use a rubric for the shared vocabulary, not as a score sheet.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or practising professionals

rows.basis: [Peer assessment](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M]: the meta-analysis includes primary students and found no reliable difference by education level; the configuration is untested
rows.change: Use two objects at a time, two or three criteria phrased as questions with picture or worked anchors, and a short spoken comparison in pairs; the teacher gives the reference each time.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (under 12)

rows.basis: [Rubric guidance](claims/rubrics-improve-peer-feedback-quality.md) [+M]: MOOC writing raters, benefit concentrated on subjective, complex criteria and negligible on simple ones
rows.change: Train raters on graded samples at each level before they judge; spend discussion time on these criteria and skip discussion of simple ones.
rows.if: The criteria are subjective or complex (quality of argument, audience fit), not simple and objective

rows.basis: [Rubric-referenced self-assessment](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [+M] (middle-school writers; pre-service teachers); [assessor benefit](claims/peer-assessment-benefits-assessor.md) [+M], correlational in its direct study
rows.change: End every session with the learner revising their own draft against the same criteria, after judging others' work; score the revision.
rows.if: The goal is better own work, not only better judgment

rows.basis: [Lateral-reading instruction](claims/civic-online-reasoning-instruction-improves-evaluation.md) [+M] (high-school and university students); [one-session checklist instruction](claims/checklist-evaluation-ineffective-online.md) [~M] did no better than the alternatives it was compared with
rows.change: Make leaving the site to check who is behind it and what others say (lateral reading) the criterion, rather than a checklist of on-page features; have the group compare what each member found off the page.
rows.if: The objects are online sources (credibility of websites, claims)

rows.basis: [Peer assessment](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M] found no difference between online and offline delivery; [the assessor-benefit meta-analysis](claims/peer-assessment-benefits-assessor.md) [+M] found computer-mediated peer assessment did better than paper. The locking and thread rules are untested
rows.change: Collect each rating in a form that locks before others' ratings are visible; reveal all together; hold the discussion in a thread limited to criteria where ratings differ by a level or more; post the reference after the thread closes.
rows.if: `online-instructor-led` or asynchronous

rows.basis: [Peer judgment accuracy](claims/peer-feedback-accuracy-depends-on-expertise.md) [~M]: with a well-specified rubric, averaged ratings by AP English students correlated with expert scores about as well as teachers' did. Correlational, one subject
rows.change: Replace group consensus with the mean of four or five independent ratings per object, and give the reference to the whole class afterwards; discuss only the objects where the mean departs most from it.
rows.if: A large class, or no teacher reaches each group

rows.basis: [Rubric use](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [~M] raised stress and a performance-avoidance orientation in pre-service teachers; [anonymous sharing](claims/anonymity-mitigates-evaluation-apprehension.md) [~W] is the authors' account, untested
rows.change: Keep collaborative evaluation formative; grade only individual judgments of new objects against the reference, or the revised own work by the teacher; make peer work anonymous.
rows.if: High stakes: peer or group ratings would count towards marks

rows.basis: [Anonymous sharing](claims/anonymity-mitigates-evaluation-apprehension.md) [~W], authors' account of one undergraduate physics course, no test
rows.change: Private written ratings first, simultaneous reveal, rotate who speaks first, and allow anonymous submission of ratings to the teacher.
rows.if: Status differences or dominant voices in groups

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: One round: two anchors of known quality, alone judgment, reveal and compare, reference, then one new object judged alone. Do not attempt co-constructed criteria.
rows.if: `single-session`, no follow-up

rows.basis: [Guided against unguided discovery](claims/guided-discovery-outperforms-pure-discovery.md) [~S]; the meta-analysis does not break results down by prior knowledge
rows.change: Teach what the instances are first; keep two or three candidate attributes and give the checklist; use only clear exemplars until the rule is stable; give feedback on each classification and state the rule soon after the induction rather than waiting for the class to find it.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain (cannot yet name the parts of an instance)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Skip the induction; give the definition and go straight to near misses and borderline cases, or ask them to generate the contrasting set.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or already use the concept

rows.basis: [Guided against unguided discovery](claims/guided-discovery-outperforms-pure-discovery.md) [~S]: 112 third- and fourth-graders learning the control-of-variables procedure; not a concept-attainment lesson
rows.change: Prefer direct instruction of the procedure with examples. Keep concept attainment for categories with visible attributes (animals, shapes).
rows.if: Learners are `child` (under 12) and the target is a procedure (e.g. a fair test)

rows.basis: [Interleaving labelled category exemplars](claims/interleaving-improves-inductive-learning.md) [~M]: benefit for paintings, photographs and mathematical tasks, reversed for word-based categories; learners' ages and settings not reported on the claim page
rows.change: Visual: after a short block of clear exemplars, mix labelled instances of the neighbouring concepts, and warn learners that practice will feel harder. Verbal: present each concept's examples together (blocked) before any mixing, keep near misses to one attribute and the labels visible. Test both on new instances.
rows.if: The concept's instances are visual or perceptual (artists' styles, rock types, skin lesions) with confusable neighbours, or verbal (word categories, sentence types such as metaphor)

rows.basis: [Rule-example sequence](claims/rule-example-sequence-efficient-rule-introduction.md) [~W] (a 1966 report of early programmed-instruction work, not a test); [the task-type argument](claims/task-type-moderates-induction-error-usefulness.md) [~W]
rows.change: State the rule, give examples, then incomplete examples to complete; use contrasting cases to compare methods.
rows.if: The target is a rule or procedure, not a category

rows.basis: [Comparing cases](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [~M]: with seventh-graders, comparing methods raised procedural knowledge and flexibility, not conceptual knowledge
rows.change: Score explanation of the attributes separately from classification, and add a self-generated non-example task.
rows.if: The outcome is conceptual explanation, not only classification

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: The system gives the yes/no label after the learner commits a written hypothesis; show the hypothesis history beside the items; end with a classification set with feedback and a stated definition.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Use concept attainment for the one or two concepts learners most often confuse; teach the rest definition-first with examples and non-examples.
rows.if: `single-session` and many concepts in the unit

rows.basis: Untested proposal (the case-comparison benefit was smaller on delayed tests, which is a reason to test late, not evidence for this pattern)
rows.change: Test on new, unlabelled instances including near misses and neighbouring concepts, at the delay that matters; do not use the practice items.
rows.if: High stakes, or assessment on new instances weeks later

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page
rows.change: Use visual or concrete instances alongside verbal ones, keep labels visible, and allow written or pointing responses so working memory is not spent on the attribute list.
rows.if: Language of instruction is not the learners' first language, or learners have reading or access needs

rows.basis: [Practice presence](claims/practice-presence-raises-cbi-posttest-achievement.md) [+M] for including practice (undergraduates, one computer-based lesson); the per-outcome dose and exemplar are untested proposals
rows.change: Add a worked or modelled example and at least one practised attempt with feedback per outcome before the graded task; show an exemplar against the criteria.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the assessed tasks

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Fewer, more integrated outcomes; assess on a realistic task in their own setting; cut practice of components they already perform.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or professionals

rows.basis: [Assessment for learning](claims/assessment-for-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+M] for formative checkpoints (K–12 syntheses); the "I can" wording is untested; the earlier page described the pattern as developed in higher education
rows.change: Write outcomes as short "I can…" statements the teacher shares and checks with learners; keep frequent low-stakes checkpoints with a revision step.
rows.if: Learners are children or adolescents (`pre-k-12`)

rows.basis: [HOCS clickers](claims/hocs-clickers-improve-locs-exam-performance.md) [~M] (one nonmajors biology course, `controlled-nonrandom`)
rows.change: Do not restrict practice to recall: include some questions at a higher level (explain, apply) in class practice.
rows.if: Goal is facts or recall (`verbal-association`) and the assessment is recall

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page. Assessor agreement is qualified on [Competency-Based Assessment](principles/competency-based-assessment.md)
rows.change: Assess a whole task with criteria and calibrated assessors; schedule whole-task practice across the course, not only at the end.
rows.if: Goal is a `complex-skill`

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the motivation claim is under Further evidence
rows.change: Do not grade it on a scale; assess the behaviour it should produce, or report it ungraded; give learners bounded choices within the aligned tasks.
rows.if: Goal is an attitude or disposition (`attitude-motivation`)

rows.basis: [Practice presence](claims/practice-presence-raises-cbi-posttest-achievement.md) [+M] (computer-based lesson, undergraduates); the audit is untested
rows.change: Build practice with immediate feedback into each module ahead of its assessed task; make criteria and exemplars part of the module; audit automatically scored items for recall-only questions.
rows.if: Setting is `online-self-paced` with no teacher present

rows.basis: [Active learning](claims/active-learning-improves-exam-performance.md) [+M] (undergraduate STEM; held across class sizes); [HOCS clickers](claims/hocs-clickers-improve-locs-exam-performance.md) [~M]
rows.change: Replace part of lecture with questions or problems answered in class that demand the outcome; use some at a higher level than the exam.
rows.if: Large lecture class, one session at a time

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page ("a single aligned lesson inside a misaligned course changes little")
rows.change: Audit the whole course, then align the one unit's outcome with an assessed item that exists; do not promise a course-level effect.
rows.if: Only one session or unit can be changed

rows.basis: [Exam questions at low levels](claims/exam-questions-concentrate-lower-bloom-levels.md) [~W] shows one university's papers sat mostly at comprehension and knowledge (`associational`); the response is an untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the outcomes you hold; add labelled practice on the examination's format; check its items' levels and record where they fall below the outcomes.
rows.if: High-stakes final assessment fixed externally

rows.basis: [Explicit instruction against unassisted discovery](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [+S]; the meta-analysis does not break results down by prior knowledge
rows.change: Keep steps 2–3 in full: explain first, two or three worked cases with explanation prompts and sentence starters before any case learners work alone; give hints in response to their explanations.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on this idea

rows.basis: [Expertise reversal](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (a review of cognitive-load studies; gives no crossover point)
rows.change: Skip the worked cases; go to boundary cases, comparison with a neighbouring idea, and use in a richer task, with selective feedback.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced`, or explain the idea correctly at step 1

rows.basis: [Misconceptions and refutation](claims/misconceptions-interfere-with-new-learning.md) [+M]; science and reading education, read from abstracts
rows.change: Make step 2 a refutation: state the wrong idea, show a case where it fails, explain why the correct idea succeeds; return to the discrepant case in later sessions and check at a delay.
rows.if: Learners hold a known, confident misconception (common in science: force and motion, seasons, heat)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the self-explanation meta-analysis spans levels of education but the claim page does not report results by age
rows.change: Keep explanation prompts short and oral or pointing-based; use concrete, visible cases; check each child's prediction individually rather than by show of hands.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (under 12)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's scope ("not sufficient for highly complex skills alone")
rows.change: Use the [Direct Instruction pattern](patterns/direct-instruction.md) or [Guided Practice](principles/guided-practice.md) instead; keep one explanation prompt per worked case at most.
rows.if: The goal is a `procedure` the learner must carry out fluently, not an idea to explain

rows.basis: [Whole-task practice](claims/whole-task-performance-improves-transfer.md) [~M] (a design argument, not a study)
rows.change: Embed the idea in a whole task from the start rather than teaching it as a separate lesson first.
rows.if: The goal is a `complex-skill` performed as a whole

rows.basis: [Comparing cases](claims/comparing-contrasting-cases-improves-learning.md) [+M]; larger effects when learners look for similarities and the principle comes after, smaller on delayed tests
rows.change: Use at least two representations and two surface-different cases; in step 5, ask learners to say what the cases share before the principle is restated.
rows.if: The outcome is transfer to new contexts

rows.basis: [Practice present in a computer-based lesson](claims/practice-presence-raises-cbi-posttest-achievement.md) [+M] (undergraduates, one lesson, horizon not reported); the explanation-comparison step is untested
rows.change: Make every prompt require a typed explanation before the next screen; give worked explanations to compare against; include automatically checked prediction items with feedback; end with an unseen changed item.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [contingent support](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M] is shown one-to-one, and its classroom-scale effect is not
rows.change: Collect step 1 predictions and step 4 checks from every learner at once (cards, mini-whiteboards, a poll); address the commonest wrong idea with the whole class, then go to those still wrong.
rows.if: `classroom` with one teacher and a large group

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Run the five steps once, keep step 5 to one comparison, and record that understanding at a delay was not checked.
rows.if: `single-session` only

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the self-explanation claim notes that evidence for delayed gains is much more limited
rows.change: Judge readiness on an unseen changed item answered unaided, not on explanations given with prompts; add the delayed check.
rows.if: High stakes, or the test is weeks away

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's guidance to vary representation and complexity
rows.change: Let learners predict and explain orally, by drawing or by choosing between given reasons before writing them; keep the representation visual; gloss terms the objective does not include.
rows.if: Instruction is in the learners' second language, or literacy is low

rows.basis: [Isolated parts first, for novices](claims/part-task-practice-reduces-load-for-novices.md) [~M] (one experiment; sample and horizon not reported on the claim page)
rows.change: Keep the epitome very short (two or three ideas); pre-teach the one or two elements it depends on in isolation, then present the epitome; make each level small and end it with a learner-built synthesis.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` and the content is `high` in element interactivity

rows.basis: untested proposal; [advance organizers](claims/advance-organizers-improve-learning.md) [~M] found no special benefit for low-knowledge learners, so neither direction of an expertise effect is established for overviews
rows.change: Replace the epitome with the elicitation sketch; start at the first level they cannot explain; drop syntheses they can already produce.
rows.if: Learners are `intermediate` or `advanced` for this content

rows.basis: [Hierarchical organisation did not help low-ability students](claims/ability-moderates-hierarchical-organization-benefit.md) [~M] (college physics volunteers; untested in other groups)
rows.change: Do not rely on the hierarchy alone: add learner-built syntheses at every level, practice tasks at each level, and a check on the top-level ideas before moving down.
rows.if: Learners have weaker prior attainment in the subject

rows.basis: untested proposal; the study tested college and advanced high-school physics students, untested with children
rows.change: Make the epitome concrete (a picture, a story or a model of the whole), keep levels to one lesson each, and have the teacher lead the synthesis aloud before asking learners to arrange items.
rows.if: Learners are `child` or `adolescent`

rows.basis: [No detected effect on tasks resting on single details](claims/no-organization-effect-on-local-tasks.md) [~M] (a non-significant difference, not equivalence)
rows.change: Do not build an elaboration sequence; use a plain grouping and retrieval practice instead.
rows.if: The goal is `verbal-association` (facts, vocabulary, names)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Sequence whole tasks with [4C/ID](patterns/4cid-four-component-instructional-design.md) and use an elaboration sequence only for the supportive information around them.
rows.if: The goal is a `complex-skill` (whole-task performance)

rows.basis: [Organisation–task match](claims/organization-task-match-determines-benefit.md) [~M] (20 high-school physics students, two-week test)
rows.change: Put the ideas that task draws on at the top of the epitome and at the top of each synthesis; assess a matched task, not a recall of the outline.
rows.if: Assessment is high-stakes and uses one kind of task (e.g. deductive problems, or historical and contextual questions)

rows.basis: [Learners explicating the organisation](claims/strong-acquisition-tasks-improve-internalization.md) [+M] for the synthesis activity (same 20-student high-school experiment; untested online); the persistent map is an untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the epitome as a persistent map on every page, with the current level highlighted; make each synthesis an activity the system checks (arrange items into the map, mark the new detail), not a passage to read.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher present

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Present the epitome and one level of elaboration only, end with one synthesis task and one application task; leave further levels for later sessions rather than compressing them.
rows.if: Time is one session (`single-session`) rather than a unit or course

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: State the epitome in short sentences with a labelled diagram; keep the same terms for the same ideas at every level; offer the synthesis as an arrange-or-label task rather than a written summary.
rows.if: Some learners study in a second language, or need accessible formats

rows.basis: [Guided against unguided discovery](claims/guided-discovery-outperforms-pure-discovery.md) [~S], carried from classroom and laboratory studies to games
rows.change: Open each session with a mentor modelling one decision aloud; one decision type per early session; feedback with the reason after every decision; fade prompts only when a learner justifies unprompted.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` to the practice

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's "transformation" games
rows.change: Skip the early modelled sessions; build the unit around two or three atypical or breakdown cases; debrief on what their usual framing missed.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` practitioners (continuing education, in-service)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Choose a practice whose decisions are visible and concrete (planning a park, running a shop); shorten sessions to 30–40 minutes; keep an adult in the mentor role; check the content separately.
rows.if: Learners are `child` or young `adolescent`

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's constraint ("overkill for simple factual or procedural learning")
rows.change: Do not build an epistemic game; teach directly with practice and feedback, and use a short simulation only for applying it.
rows.if: The goal is facts or a procedure, not judgement

rows.basis: [Simulation training in the health professions](claims/simulation-based-education-improves-outcomes.md) [+M] (against no training); [practice-near content](claims/contextualized-teaching-facilitates-transfer.md) [+W] (nurses' perceptions)
rows.change: Use cases drawn from the learners' own workplace, a practitioner as mentor, and an outside-game task that matches a real work task; record transfer to work separately from in-game performance.
rows.if: `adult-workplace` learners in `workplace-clinical` training

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [feedback](claims/feedback-improves-learning.md) [+S] carried to software feedback
rows.change: Mentor characters must carry all guidance: a modelled decision before each new decision type, required written justification, scripted feedback with reasons, and a written debrief prompt at the end of each session. Expect weaker debriefs than with a person.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep the world playable in a browser on a phone (documents and decisions as text and images, no heavy 3D); give remote learners a named role with their own documents so the team must consult them; run the debrief in a shared document everyone writes in.
rows.if: Mixed mode: some learners in the room, some joining remotely, or phone-only

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the earlier page's role differentiation
rows.change: Run in teams of four with differentiated roles (departments); the teacher plays one mentor character for the whole class at set points, and teams check decisions against a written checklist from the epistemography between visits.
rows.if: One teacher or practitioner for many learners (30 or more)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [Communities of Practice](principles/communities-of-practice.md) notes norms take a term to form
rows.change: Drop the full game: one case, one role, a modelled decision, one learner decision with feedback, and a 15-minute debrief on the frame. Do not expect a change in identity from one session.
rows.if: `single-session` only (one workshop)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Give the world's documents as short texts with audio and images; start with low-stakes decisions whose consequences can be undone; let learners justify orally or by choosing among stated reasons.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or low literacy

rows.basis: Untested here; see [Authentic Assessment](patterns/authentic-assessment.md) and [Authentic Audiences and Purposes](principles/authentic-audiences-purposes.md)
rows.change: Keep the fiction's audience real: practitioners or residents read the final plan and respond; share their criteria at the brief; build a draft-review-revise step before the presentation.
rows.if: The final product goes to a real audience (a council, a client, a community group)

rows.basis: [Reliability is hard to define in epistemic games](claims/reliability-challenges-epistemic-games.md) [~W] (an argument); [longer play separated simulated learner types better](claims/longer-games-sharpen-wd-learner-differentiation.md) [~W] (simulated learners, not real ones)
rows.change: Grade the final product and an outside-game case against public criteria with two raters, not the play log; if the log is scored, play long enough to accumulate evidence and keep few, broad dimensions.
rows.if: The game will be used for high-stakes grading

rows.basis: [Disciplinary differences went unnoticed](claims/epistemic-games-reveal-unacknowledged-disciplinary-differences-in-teams.md) [~W]; [a shared outline turned unfocused talk into structured work](claims/organization-simulation-knowledge-practices-support-interdisciplinary-learning.md) [+W]; both descriptive, neither tests the move
rows.change: Ask each member at the start to state what evidence would convince them and when a framing is "done"; revisit it in the debrief; give the team a shared visible plan (flip chart, board).
rows.if: Interdisciplinary teams

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [the simulation synthesis](claims/simulation-based-education-improves-outcomes.md) [+M] found no consistent design feature, and fidelity was not among those it recorded
rows.change: Use a paper or document-based simulation (briefs, letters, maps, a budget sheet) with a teacher in role, rather than software; spend the budget on the epistemography.
rows.if: Little budget or time to build a world

rows.basis: [Activation](claims/activation-improves-learning.md) [~S] and [activation instructions](claims/prior-knowledge-activation-little-effect-on-retention.md) [~M]: topic activation alone did not help (primary pupils; one other experiment), carried to this routine
rows.change: Give the meaning of key terms and the gist first; make step 2 a checked account (compare with the text) rather than free recall; give a stem for every step for longer (sessions 1–5); correct each "learned" answer against the named idea.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the content, or the text is hard for them

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Make steps 2 and 3 implicit; spend the time on step 5, with learners generating questions and choosing the next source to answer them.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` in the content

rows.basis: [Writing to learn](claims/writing-to-learn-improves-understanding.md) [~S]: effects were reduced in grades 6–8 and with longer assignments (a moderator in one meta-analysis, read from its abstract)
rows.change: Keep writing short (one or two sentences per step), answer steps 2 and 3 orally, and write only step 4.
rows.if: Learners are in grades 6–8, or young `child` writers

rows.basis: [Specific reflection prompts](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+S] (engineering undergraduates; school writing-to-learn studies)
rows.change: Write a content-specific step 4 prompt for each session and score the answer against the named idea; keep the number of reflections constant rather than adding more.
rows.if: The goal is understanding of a `concept` or `principle` in a course

rows.basis: [Self-questioning](claims/self-questioning-improves-comprehension.md) [+S] (K–12 reading; reviews read from abstracts)
rows.change: Teach step 5 as question generation during reading as well as after it: model it, give stems, fade them.
rows.if: The goal is reading comprehension of content texts

rows.basis: Untested; the source's structured-discussion vocabulary routine ([strategy page](strategies/structured-discussion-vocabulary-anchoring.md))
rows.change: For each new term, give the meaning and an example first, then ask "What experiences, thoughts or associations do you have with this term that might help you remember it?"; learners record the dictionary meaning and a personal association.
rows.if: The goal is vocabulary

rows.basis: [Task value](claims/task-value-increases-motivation-and-engagement.md) [+M]: brief utility-value writing raised engagement and grades (two reviews); a separate intervention, carried to this step
rows.change: Weight step 3 towards usefulness: "How could this matter to you or to people you know?", two sentences, ungraded.
rows.if: Learners see no point in the content, or are from groups underrepresented in the subject

rows.basis: [Specific reflection prompts](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+S] and [guided reflection](claims/guided-reflection-yields-more-higher-order-paragraphs-than-free.md) [+M], carried from undergraduates and graduate students to workplace learners
rows.change: Use a recent work incident or case as the experience; make step 4 a statement of what they would do differently and why; make step 5 a question to take to a colleague or the next shift.
rows.if: Adults in work settings (`adult-workplace`, `workplace-clinical`)

rows.basis: [Metacognitive prompts](claims/metacognitive-prompts-improve-learning.md) [+S]: in computer-based environments prompts helped, more so with feedback, task-specific and adaptive (meta-analysis read from its abstract)
rows.change: Embed the four prompts after each segment; after the learner commits a step 4 answer, show a model answer and ask them to mark what they missed; adapt the stem to the content of the segment.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no teacher

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Take every written answer in one shared channel (a shared document or chat) so remote and in-room answers are seen together; keep phone answers to one or two sentences; let remote learners answer step 3 privately.
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners remote, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: Untested; the "why did you choose this correct answer" move is the source's ([strategy page](strategies/question-correct-answers-not-errors.md))
rows.change: Have learners write steps 4 and 5; the facilitator reads a sample of five step 4 answers and responds to the whole group, asking one learner why a correct answer is correct; pairs check each other's answer against a model answer.
rows.if: One teacher for many learners, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, a tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Run one cycle on one experience; end with each learner's step 5 question written on an exit card and answered in a short follow-up message or handout.
rows.if: `single-session` only

rows.basis: Untested; from the source's precepts (students fail from too little information; the teacher as a model of language and inquiry)
rows.change: Answer steps 2 and 3 orally in pairs or in the first language; give a sentence frame for step 4; respond first to what is right in an answer; never read personal responses aloud without consent.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or low literacy in the language of instruction

rows.basis: [Specific reflection prompts](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+S], on prompt specificity, not on any named routine
rows.change: Keep it. Change only what the evidence says matters: make sure one item asks for the content idea with a content-specific prompt and is checked, and that one item asks what more needs to be known.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine for this (a KWL chart, "What? So what? Now what?", a journal template)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Turn step 4 answers into a short public explanation for that audience, written after the content check, and step 5 questions into the questions the product sets out to answer.
rows.if: The answers feed a product or performance for a real audience

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Score the step 4 answer against the content idea separately from the personal response; retest the idea on a new example after a delay; do not grade step 3.
rows.if: High stakes, or understanding must hold weeks later

rows.basis: [Guided against unassisted discovery](claims/guided-discovery-outperforms-pure-discovery.md) [~S]; discovery tasks with mostly school learners and mixed domains, not placements or simulations; the meta-analysis does not break results down by prior knowledge
rows.change: Demonstrate the first loop's task with a worked example before the experience; let one or two variables vary; supply the debrief prompts and the vocabulary for stating the principle; check each learner's rule before the retry; keep this support for at least the first two loops.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` on the target task

rows.basis: Untested; the guided-discovery claim's narrative review argues the advantage of guidance recedes with prior knowledge, which no recorded study tests here
rows.change: Skip the demonstration; make the first experience ill-structured; have learners write their own debrief questions from the first loop; keep the changed attempt with feedback.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or experienced practitioners

rows.basis: [Hands-on learning](claims/hands-on-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+M] (mathematics manipulatives, kindergarten to college); [guided against unassisted discovery](claims/guided-discovery-outperforms-pure-discovery.md) [~S] (third and fourth graders learning a procedure); loop lengths untested
rows.change: Shorter loops (experience 10–15 minutes, debrief 5 minutes); concrete materials linked to the written or symbolic form in the same session; tell them what to try rather than only to explore; the teacher states the rule.
rows.if: Learners are `child`ren (under 12)

rows.basis: [Simulation with deliberate practice](claims/simulation-based-education-with-deliberate-practice-improves-clinical-outcomes.md) [+M]; medical education, procedural skills only
rows.change: Run the experience as simulated practice repeated to a stated mastery standard, feedback after each attempt, rising difficulty, then a debrief; move to the real setting only when the standard is met.
rows.if: `workplace-clinical`, a `procedure` or psychomotor skill

rows.basis: [Physical experience](claims/physical-experience-enhances-science-learning.md) [~M] (undergraduate physics; physical and virtual manipulation equally effective); [cognitive conflict](claims/cognitive-disequilibrium-motivates-conceptual-change.md) [+M] (science-education conceptual-change strategies)
rows.change: Make the experience a predict-then-manipulate task (physical or virtual), with a stated prediction before acting, and map the result onto the formula or diagram during the principle step; use a virtual lab when a physical one is not available.
rows.if: The goal is a science or mathematics `concept`

rows.basis: [Experiential learning benefits reported in human services education](claims/experiential-learning-engagement-skills-ethical-reasoning.md) [+W], second-hand, no design or effect size; otherwise untested
rows.change: Use cases or placements with structured debriefs; assess a decision on a new case observed later, not a journal; treat any self-reported gain as unconfirmed.
rows.if: The goal is professional judgement or a disposition

rows.basis: [Structured reflection](claims/reflective-practice-improves-outcomes-when-structured.md) [+M] for written specific prompts (a classroom engineering course); untested online
rows.change: Replace the live debrief with three written prompts after each task and a model answer to compare against; offer an automatically scored changed task as the retry.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no facilitator

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's compressed-timeframe guidance
rows.change: One complete loop: a 15-minute experience, a 10-minute written debrief, a stated rule, one changed attempt; no second loop.
rows.if: `single-session`

rows.basis: Untested; [reflection in higher education](claims/reflective-practice-evidence-mixed-in-professional-education.md) [~M] reports peer interaction as a moderator, direction not stated on the claim page
rows.change: Debrief in pairs or threes against a written protocol; spend facilitator time on checking stated principles, where a wrong rule is hardest for peers to catch.
rows.if: Large cohort, one facilitator

rows.basis: [Learning-style matching](claims/learning-styles-matching-does-not-improve-learning.md) [-S]; [Kolb styles unchanged over a year](claims/kolb-learning-style-stable-over-one-year.md) [-W] and [no link to career choice](claims/kolb-inventory-limited-validity-career-and-personality.md) [-W], both second-hand reports in one review
rows.change: Drop the style diagnosis and the matching; run every learner through every stage.
rows.if: The program bundles the cycle with Kolb's Learning Style Inventory, or asks to start learners at their "preferred stage"

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's constraint that graded reflection becomes a compliance artifact
rows.change: Assess the changed attempt and a new unaided task; do not grade journals for completion; score principle and performance separately.
rows.if: Credit attaches to reflection, or assessment is high-stakes

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's personalization
rows.change: Written or recorded reflection, in the language they choose, before any group debrief; sentence starters for the prompts.
rows.if: Learners are uncomfortable reflecting in public, or reflect in a second language

rows.basis: [Guided against unguided discovery](claims/guided-discovery-outperforms-pure-discovery.md) [~S]: explicit instruction beat unassisted discovery, guided discovery beat other instruction; the meta-analysis does not break results down by prior knowledge, and is not of this pattern
rows.change: Teach the core ideas directly before research; give each research group a short, pre-selected source pack and a note frame; check each group's understanding before jigsaw.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the domain

rows.basis: [Reciprocal teaching](claims/reciprocal-teaching-improves-reading-comprehension.md) [+M] (16 studies); [especially poor readers](claims/reciprocal-teaching-raises-reading-comprehension-poor-readers.md) [+W] (a narrative review citing one study). Neither tests the whole pattern
rows.change: Make reciprocal teaching the main activity of research, with the teacher leading one group per session and modelling each move for several sessions before handing over; keep subtopics to three.
rows.if: Learners are younger readers, or struggling readers, in `primary` school

rows.basis: [Secondary review](claims/secondary-cooperative-learning-newmann-thompson.md) [~M]: only 33% of grade 10–12 studies were successful and jigsaw was least successful; [group rewards on individual learning](claims/cooperative-learning-group-rewards-and-individual-accountability.md) [+M]
rows.change: Do not rely on jigsaw alone: add team recognition built from individual quiz results, and a structured teaching protocol.
rows.if: Learners are in upper `secondary` (grades 10–12)

rows.basis: [Small-group learning in undergraduate STEM](claims/small-group-learning-improves-stem-achievement.md) [+M] (d = 0.51 against non-group instruction; does not separate structured from unstructured groups)
rows.change: Use the cycle for one unit a term; groups of 3–4; individual checks each week; keep lectures for core ideas.
rows.if: `postsecondary` STEM course

rows.basis: [Communities of practice principle](principles/communities-of-practice.md), whose evidence is descriptive; [mathematics PLC review](claims/plc-participation-changes-teacher-norms-understanding-practice.md) [+M] (a review of descriptive studies, no comparison)
rows.change: Make the theme a recurring problem of practice; each member researches a case or source and teaches it back; the shared task is a protocol or guide the team will use; observe practice afterwards, not only self-report.
rows.if: Adults in a work setting (a professional learning cohort, `workplace-clinical`)

rows.basis: Untested; reciprocal teaching's claim page says the routine needs sustained practice over multiple sessions
rows.change: Do not attempt the full pattern. Run one jigsaw on pre-read material with a teaching protocol and an individual check on every part; leave reciprocal-teaching handover out.
rows.if: `single-session` only

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Put each remote learner in a research group with at least one other remote learner or give the group a shared online document and audio channel; in jigsaw, the remote expert teaches from a shared screen with the protocol visible; collect individual checks online for everyone.
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners remote, some in the room

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [learning by teaching](claims/learning-by-teaching-improves-tutor-learning.md) [~M] found interactive teaching better than non-interactive, so expect less benefit without live questions
rows.change: Replace live jigsaw with asynchronous teaching: each expert posts a short explanation and two questions; peers answer and the expert replies; an automatic individual quiz on every part decides progress.
rows.if: `online-self-paced` or phone-only, no live sessions

rows.basis: [Contingent scaffolding](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [~M]: evidence mostly from one-to-one tutoring; its claim page notes contingency across a whole class is hard. The rota is untested
rows.change: Use role cards and question stems so groups can run without the teacher; the teacher circulates on a fixed rota and checks each research group once before jigsaw; use written exit checks to decide which group to visit.
rows.if: One teacher for many groups (30+ learners)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [positioning learners as sources](claims/positioning-students-as-sources-increases-productive-participation-in-science-discourse.md) [+M] widened participation in one lower-secondary science class (qualitative, no comparison group)
rows.change: Give each learner a defined, bounded role (questioner, summariser) and a rehearsal with the research group before teaching; let experts teach in pairs; accept spoken or drawn explanations in checks.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence or low literacy

rows.basis: [Group rewards on individual learning](claims/cooperative-learning-group-rewards-and-individual-accountability.md) [+M]; reciprocal teaching's [gap between standardised and researcher-written tests](claims/reciprocal-teaching-improves-reading-comprehension.md) [~M] is a reason to check with an independent measure
rows.change: Score every learner on every subtopic, add a teacher-led review of parts where peer-taught scores lag, and test at the delay that matters.
rows.if: High stakes: an individual exam on all content

rows.basis: Untested proposal; extends the earlier page's step of creating artifacts and sharing findings
rows.change: Make it the shared task in step 6 and name the audience at launch; still score individual understanding separately from the product.
rows.if: A product or performance for a real audience (an exhibition, a guide for younger pupils, a report for a partner)

rows.basis: [Minimal guidance and novices](claims/minimal-guidance-less-effective-for-novices.md) [~S]; tested on discovery and inquiry, carried to production
rows.change: Teach the essential content explicitly first (step 2), provide the sources, use a blueprint template with one scene filled in, fix the product to 2 minutes, and check content individually before production.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the content

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Skip the content investigation to a short review; spend the time on exemplars and media criteria; let learners choose the audience and write their own criteria.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` in the content but new to the media

rows.basis: Untested; the audience comparison with second graders ([authentic audiences](claims/authentic-audiences-improve-student-work.md) [+M]) concerned writing, not media
rows.change: One medium (narrated pictures, a poster with audio), roles named with pictures, the teacher scribes the storyboard, sessions of 30–40 minutes, and an audience they know (another class, families).
rows.if: Learners are `child` (primary age)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [learning by teaching](claims/learning-by-teaching-improves-tutor-learning.md) [+M] supports making each learner explain their part, not tested with adults at work
rows.change: Make the product something colleagues will use (a 2-minute procedure video, a job aid), with a subject-matter expert reviewing the blueprint for accuracy before recording; individual check on the procedure itself.
rows.if: Learners are `adult` in a work setting (`workplace-clinical`, onboarding, professional development)

rows.basis: [Learner-constructed organizers did worse on transfer](claims/learner-constructed-graphic-organizers-outperform-provided.md) [~M], college readers of a text, carried by analogy
rows.change: Cap production at a third of the unit's time, use the simplest medium that carries the content, score content apart from polish, and run the individual content check at a delay.
rows.if: The goal is subject content; media literacy is incidental

rows.basis: [Interdisciplinary humanities units](claims/interdisciplinary-humanities-units-improve-interdisciplinary-competences.md) [+M]: one non-randomized middle-school study; units, not media production
rows.change: Plan the product with two subject teachers, each owning content criteria on the blueprint; ask for one scene that connects the two subjects explicitly.
rows.if: The goal includes cross-curricular or interdisciplinary learning

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the project-based meta-analysis ([project-based learning](claims/project-based-learning-improves-achievement.md) [+M]) excludes short single activities
rows.change: Drop production of new media: teams annotate or re-sequence provided clips or slides into a 1-minute explanation, present to another team, and answer one question each.
rows.if: `single-session` only

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Give remote members roles that work on a phone (script, narration, research, still photos); keep the blueprint in one shared document; present by screen share with questions in chat, and run the individual check in writing for everyone.
rows.if: Mixed mode: some learners remote, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: Untested proposal; the blueprint check is the step most directly tied to the [content-quality concern](claims/learner-constructed-graphic-organizers-outperform-provided.md) [~M]
rows.change: Spend the facilitator's minutes on two checks only: the blueprint's content (5 minutes per team) and the individual explanation before presentation. Teams peer-review blueprints against the criteria list first; use templates so tool questions do not reach the facilitator.
rows.if: One teacher for many teams, or scarce facilitator time (volunteers, a busy shift, a tutor checking in briefly)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Allow pictures and speech instead of written text in the product and blueprint; give sentence frames for narration; let a learner present in a small group or by recording; keep the individual content check oral.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence, low literacy, or learning in a second language

rows.basis: [Authentic audiences](claims/authentic-audiences-improve-student-work.md) [+M] (product quality on writing); the [authentic audiences principle](principles/authentic-audiences-purposes.md) holds the conditions
rows.change: Agree with the audience what they need and whether they will respond; plan time to revise after their response; score the content against criteria and record the audience's reaction separately; get consent for anything public.
rows.if: The product goes to a real audience (a community partner, families, a public site)

rows.basis: [Rubric self-assessment](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [~M], with its stress and avoidance finding; [the grading argument for maker education](claims/grading-harms-maker-education-outcomes.md) [~W], an argument, not a test
rows.change: Grade content understanding individually as well as the team product; publish the criteria from the start; consider weighting process evidence (blueprint, revisions).
rows.if: High stakes: the product is graded for a qualification

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep it. Change only what the evidence says matters: add a content point per scene to the template, separate content from media rows on the rubric, and add one individual content check before presentation.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (its own storyboard template, rubric, production checklist or presentation format)

rows.basis: Untested; from the earlier page's "handmade TV program" example
rows.change: Make the product live rather than recorded (a performance, a gallery walk, a radio-style reading), or record on one device in turn while other teams plan and rehearse.
rows.if: Little equipment (one device per class, no editing software)

rows.basis: Untested here. The [SRL synthesis](claims/srl-interventions-moderate-effect-online-blended.md) [+M] does not break results down by prior knowledge
rows.change: Put more of each week into the content strand, with worked examples and self-checks, and keep discussion tasks to applying what was just shown; give feedback on every early piece.
rows.if: Learners are `novice` in the content

rows.basis: [Template and organisation ratings](claims/course-template-supports-learner-presence.md) [+W] from one accelerated online MBA, descriptive; the rest is the earlier page's guidance
rows.change: Use their work as the discussion material (cases from their own settings), let them facilitate earlier, and keep the content strand short; keep the fixed structure.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or practitioners (an MBA, a professional course)

rows.basis: [Online community required deliberate, planned effort](claims/online-community-requires-conscious-effort.md) [+W] (interviews with high-school e-teachers); the actions are untested
rows.change: Plan every interaction and the community-building explicitly; schedule live contact; keep the weekly structure strict and contact families or a school mentor after a missed week.
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent` in a web-based school course

rows.basis: [Implementation intentions](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [+S] (the two field experiments were in large online courses); the rest is untested
rows.change: Replace teacher feedback on each piece with automatic feedback on self-checks, a weekly teacher summary of common errors, and peer review against a rubric; keep the week-1 if-then plan; give the teacher's time to learners flagged by a missed week.
rows.if: `online-self-paced` with rolling enrolment, or one teacher for hundreds of learners

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Give remote learners their own small groups, or mixed groups that all work in the same online space, rather than letting the room talk and the remote learners listen; one person watches the online channel in every live session; post every product online.
rows.if: Some learners join from a shared room while others are remote (hyflex), or a site group joins a remote teacher

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Keep each content segment short and downloadable, give transcripts, allow text or voice replies in discussion, and avoid tasks that need a large screen; make live sessions optional with a recording and a written summary.
rows.if: Phone-only learners or low bandwidth

rows.basis: [Discussion board produced no corrective feedback](claims/discussion-board-no-negative-feedback-synchrony-required.md) [~M], one second-language study carried to other subjects
rows.change: Use a short recorded or written teacher reply in week 1 instead of a call; put corrective feedback into written comments on each graded piece, since asynchronous boards may surface no correction.
rows.if: No live sessions possible (time zones, shift work)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Cut the cycle to one content block and one discussion task a week; shorten the opening contact to the first two days; keep feedback within 48 hours, since there is no time to recover a missed week. In a one-week or single-session module, drop the group progression and use one structured task with a shared product.
rows.if: Accelerated term (6–8 weeks) or a single short module

rows.basis: [Implementation intentions](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [+S] (MCII helped most when the obstacle was predictable, such as work or family obligations); [withdrawal reasons](claims/withdrawal-reasons-similar-across-modalities.md) [~M] were led by no stated reason, transfer and schedule conflict in one programme
rows.change: Publish the full term's due dates in week 1; make the if-then plan name a work or family obstacle; offer a reduced catch-up route after a missed week.
rows.if: Adults in work settings, studying around jobs and family

rows.basis: [Implementation intentions](claims/implementation-intentions-improve-goal-attainment.md) [~S]: no effect on completion for learners in collectivist cultures in the field experiments
rows.change: Do not rely on the if-then plan alone; add the week-1 contact and early follow-up on missed weeks, and record completion by group.
rows.if: Learners from collectivist cultures, or the course depends on completion for its funding

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Give each week's page in plain language, a short video walk-through of the structure in week 1, sentence starters and model posts, and private channels for questions; let first contributions be in small groups, not the whole class.
rows.if: Learners with low confidence, reading difficulty or a first language other than the course's

rows.basis: [Discussion board produced no corrective feedback](claims/discussion-board-no-negative-feedback-synchrony-required.md) [~M]
rows.change: Hold a weekly synchronous session (text chat or video) for practice with correction; use the board for reflection and preparation.
rows.if: A language course, or any goal where errors must be corrected

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Make the group products build towards it across the term, with drafts reviewed by peers and the teacher, and plan a live or recorded presentation to the audience in the final week; keep individual assessment of each learner's part.
rows.if: The course ends in a product or performance for a real audience (a client, a public showcase)

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Assess the representative task individually and under conditions close to the real one; do not count discussion participation towards more than a small share of the grade; report completion beside achievement.
rows.if: High stakes: a credential, licensure or a programme-required course

rows.basis: [Blended and online against face-to-face](claims/blended-learning-improves-outcomes.md) [~M]: the blended advantage came with extra time and resources
rows.change: Record what besides the mode changed (time, materials, assessment, teacher) and compare like with like; do not credit the format with a gain.
rows.if: The course is to be compared with its face-to-face version

rows.basis: [Interdependence type did not affect achievement](claims/interdependence-type-no-achievement-effect-asynchronous.md) [-M]; [reward interdependence raised positive attitudes to group work](claims/reward-interdependence-benefit-attitudes.md) [~M], both one experiment with undergraduate business majors
rows.change: Use a group product and a task that needs everyone's input; use roles to organise, not as the source of learning, and grade individual performance.
rows.if: Group work is required and the brief proposes roles or a group grade to make it work

rows.basis: [Contingent support](claims/contingent-scaffolding-improves-learning.md) [+M] and [fading](claims/fading-support-promotes-transfer-of-responsibility.md) [+M], from students, carried to teachers; doses untested
rows.change: Keep the coach or mentor modeling in the teacher's own class for longer, observe weekly, debrief within a day, and fade only after two consecutive lessons at the agreed level; focus on one routine (often classroom management) at a time.
rows.if: New teachers in their first years, or student teachers on placement

rows.basis: [Expertise reversal](claims/expertise-reversal-effect.md) [~M] (trainees and students, not teachers); [content familiarity, not experience, predicted reform practice](claims/content-familiarity-predicts-reform-practice-experience-does-not.md) [~M] (one association study)
rows.change: Shorten modeling; start from the points where their current routine and the new practice clash; offer the principle and exemplars rather than a script; let them choose the video segment from the first cycle. Do not assume resistance from experience.
rows.if: Experienced teachers adopting a new practice or curriculum

rows.basis: [Content familiarity predicted reform practice](claims/content-familiarity-predicts-reform-practice-experience-does-not.md) [~M]: an association, not a test of content PD
rows.change: Add content study to the PD (doing the students' tasks as learners, then analysing them) before coaching the routine.
rows.if: Teachers with weak content knowledge in the subject the practice serves

rows.basis: [Buy-in is seen as mediating coaching](claims/teacher-buy-in-mediates-coaching-benefit.md) [~W]; [changed timing, offerings and credit drew in earlier non-participants](claims/nonparticipant-barriers-professional-development.md) [~W] (one program)
rows.change: Use video of colleagues of similar standing rather than expert demonstrators; start with a small practice that can succeed in one lesson; keep coaching separate from appraisal; offer timing and credit that suit them.
rows.if: Teachers with low confidence, or a team reluctant to take part

rows.basis: [Minimal success designing Constructive and Interactive activities after ICAP PD](claims/teachers-struggle-designing-interactive-activities.md) [-M]
rows.change: Make lesson design the practiced task: co-plan, get feedback on the plan, then enact and debrief. Do not expect a knowledge course to produce it.
rows.if: The target is teachers designing their own lessons with a framework, not running given ones

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [coaching aimed at a specific academic task](claims/coaching-academic-task-fidelity-higher-quality.md) [+M] supports narrowing the target, not the shortened format
rows.change: Coach one practice at a time; replace live observation with a 5–10 minute teacher-chosen video clip and a 20-minute debrief; run rehearsal and later cycles in pairs or trios with peer observers; give the coach's time to the teachers whose observed enactment is furthest from the target.
rows.if: One coach for many teachers, or scarce facilitator time (a coach across several schools, a busy term)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; [video self-observation](claims/video-self-observation-powerful-coaching-component.md) [+W] (web-mediated coaching, teachers' reports)
rows.change: Make filmed lessons the shared object for everyone; post clips before the meeting so remote teachers view them as the room does; pair each remote teacher with an in-room partner for rehearsal; debrief online within two school days.
rows.if: Some teachers join remotely while others are in the room, or coaching is wholly online

rows.basis: [Half of inservice activities lasted four hours or less, mostly talks or brief workshops](claims/expert-presenter-model-most-prevalent.md) [~W] (prevalence, not effect); [short, fragmented training is reported to hinder a holistic view](claims/systemic-approach-in-service-teacher-education.md) [-W]; the follow-up is untested
rows.change: Use it to model and rehearse one narrow practice and to set up a follow-up the school can run without the presenter: one peer observation with a look-for list within two weeks and one team meeting to review the clips. Do not promise changed practice from the session alone.
rows.if: Only a single session is available (an inset day, a one-off workshop)

rows.basis: Untested in this form; [coaching aimed at a specific academic task](claims/coaching-academic-task-fidelity-higher-quality.md) [+M]; [maintenance rarely measured](claims/coaching-maintenance-rarely-measured.md) [~M]
rows.change: Keep it; change only what the evidence says matters: make sure its focus is one observable practice, that feedback follows an enactment with students, and that one observation happens after support ends.
rows.if: The brief names its own routine (a district observation rubric, a PLC protocol, a lesson-study cycle, a coaching model already in use)

rows.basis: [Supervisory coaching shows mixed effects](claims/supervisory-coaching-mixed-teacher-student-outcomes.md) [~M] (16 K–12 studies, 6 met all quality indicators)
rows.change: Separate the coaching record from appraisal, or name plainly what the supervisor will see; expect mixed results and measure both teacher and student change.
rows.if: Coaching is run by supervisors or is tied to performance evaluation

rows.basis: [Leader-teacher diffusion was uneven](claims/leader-teacher-diffusion-uneven.md) [~M] (one three-year program)
rows.change: Give lead teachers released time, principal support, and their own coaching on how to coach; plan for uneven spread and observe colleagues' practice, not the lead teachers' only.
rows.if: Scaling through lead teachers or train-the-trainer

rows.basis: [Hunter's ITIP lacked evidence of improved achievement as implemented under typical conditions](claims/itip-lacks-empirical-evidence-achievement.md) [-M] (a review reported second-hand)
rows.change: Pilot with observation of practice and a student measure before scaling; budget follow-up coaching rather than more presenter days.
rows.if: District- or statewide rollout of one PD model to all schools

rows.basis: Untested; the coaching claims are from K–12 classrooms
rows.change: Use the same cycle with a peer observer from the same department; let the observed session be a seminar, lab or online class; time the cycle to the teaching calendar (one cycle per three or four weeks of teaching).
rows.if: Higher-education faculty, teaching assistants or adult-education tutors (adults in work settings with little release time)

rows.basis: Untested proposal; see [lesson study](strategies/lesson-study.md)
rows.change: Use it as the end of the arc: the team plans, teaches and revises one research lesson observed by colleagues, with the debrief about students' responses, not the teacher's performance.
rows.if: A real audience for the teachers' work (a public research lesson, a showcase, a conference)

rows.basis: [Early-childhood SEL synthesis](claims/sel-programs-improve-social-emotional-skills.md) [+S]: 63 studies of universal curricula in centres; the play-based format and lesson length are untested proposals
rows.change: Teach through play, picture emotion cards and puppets; lessons of 10–15 minutes; adults name emotions as they happen; measure social and emotional competence by observation and more than one informant.
rows.if: Learners are aged 2–6, in an early-childhood centre

rows.basis: [Autonomy support](claims/autonomy-supports-intrinsic-motivation.md) [~M], carried from intrinsic motivation to SEL; [mindfulness programmes](claims/mindfulness-programs-benefit-adolescent-regulation.md) [+W] and [self-regulation interventions with high schoolers and young adults](claims/sr-interventions-improve-cognitive-regulation-young-adults.md) [+W], one practice brief's review, no effect sizes
rows.change: Frame skills around fairness, identity, friendship and real stakes; let learners choose scenarios and lead discussion; avoid scripts that feel young; offer mindfulness or breathing practice as one strategy among several.
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent`

rows.basis: Untested: no claim here tests SEL with adults; the examples are the earlier page's
rows.change: Present the skills as professional competence; use cases and structured reflective discussion of real encounters (Balint-style groups) instead of scripted lessons; assess on observed practice.
rows.if: `adult` learners in work settings (health care, teaching, management, customer service)

rows.basis: [SEL and achievement](claims/sel-programs-improve-behavior-and-achievement.md) [~S]: small at post-test in the older synthesis (significant only with school-staff delivery), negligible in randomised trials of a recent one, larger for GPA
rows.change: Keep SEL, but embed the skills in academic lessons, delivered by the subject teacher, and promise only a small achievement effect; measure achievement on an independent test, not the programme's own.
rows.if: The goal is academic achievement

rows.basis: [SEL and achievement](claims/sel-programs-improve-behavior-and-achievement.md) [~S] and [SEL skills](claims/sel-programs-improve-social-emotional-skills.md) [~S]: delivery by non-school personnel and multicomponent programmes showed weaker or non-significant effects
rows.change: Train and involve the class teacher, who cues the skill daily; or, failing that, expect smaller effects and measure them.
rows.if: An outside provider or a pull-out session will deliver it

rows.basis: [Empathy-building claim](claims/building-empathy-improves-intergroup-attitudes.md) [~M]: most prejudice-reduction studies test light-touch interventions with unclear long-term effects; [empathic discipline](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [+M]: a brief teacher exercise reduced suspensions for high-risk groups, with a marginal overall effect in the preregistered replication
rows.change: Do not promise durable change. Teach one skill and leave a routine (a check-in card, a breathing step) the teacher will run daily; or spend the session on the adults' discipline mindset instead.
rows.if: A single session, assembly or workshop only

rows.basis: [Empathic discipline](claims/brief-intervention-empathic-discipline-cuts-suspensions.md) [+M] (middle-school mathematics teachers); [positive greetings](claims/positive-greetings-at-the-door-improve-engagement.md) [+M] (middle school, engagement and disruption)
rows.change: Add a short empathic-discipline exercise for teachers and a daily greeting routine before or alongside the student programme; track exclusions by group.
rows.if: Exclusions, suspensions or disruption are the presenting problem

rows.basis: [Follow-up evidence](claims/sel-benefits-persist-follow-up.md) [+S]: a preschool SEL and language programme for low-income children showed young-adult advantages 17 years later and buffered adverse childhood experiences; the privacy rule is untested
rows.change: Start with regulation and predictability before social sharing; keep emotional disclosure private and optional; plan for multiple years.
rows.if: Many learners live with adversity, poverty or chronic stress

rows.basis: [Emotion labelling](claims/emotion-labeling-improves-regulation.md) [~M], carried from fearful adults in a clinical laboratory; the visual supports are untested
rows.change: Use visual emotion scales and choice cards; teach the emotion words directly; allow pointing or drawing in check-ins; extend practice cycles.
rows.if: Learners use a language other than the language of instruction, or have low literacy

rows.basis: [Follow-up synthesis](claims/sel-benefits-persist-follow-up.md) [~S]: benefits similar across race, socioeconomic status and school location (abstract); adaptation itself is untested
rows.change: Adapt scenarios, emotion vocabulary and norms for expression with families and learners; keep the explicit, active, sequenced structure.
rows.if: The programme was designed in another country or culture

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Run the skill lesson whole-class with paired rehearsal and cue cards; use a 2-minute written check-in instead of a sharing circle; coach a few learners each day in rotation.
rows.if: One teacher with a large class (30+) and little time

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Run check-ins as a private poll or chat message so remote learners are seen equally; pair each remote learner with one in the room for rehearsal (breakout or phone call); send the week's skill as a short text with one practice task.
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners remote, some in the room, or phone-only

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Use short video models and private reflection prompts; ask learners to log one real use of the skill a week; add a human contact (tutor message, peer partner) where possible, since coaching and modelling in the moment cannot happen.
rows.if: `online-self-paced`, no adult present

rows.basis: [Group rewards on individual learning](claims/cooperative-learning-group-rewards-and-individual-accountability.md) [~M], carried from achievement in cooperative methods; the audience format is untested
rows.change: Rehearse the exact interaction first with role-play and feedback; give each learner an individual role they are accountable for; debrief privately after.
rows.if: Learners will run something for a real audience (peer mediation, a family evening, mentoring younger pupils)

rows.basis: [Early-childhood synthesis](claims/sel-programs-improve-social-emotional-skills.md) [~S]: effects varied by informant and assessment type; [emotion labelling](claims/emotion-labeling-improves-regulation.md) [~M]: the physiological measure moved when self-report did not
rows.change: Add an observed or teacher-rated measure and a conduct record; report each separately.
rows.if: The evaluation relies on student self-report

rows.basis: untested proposal; [argumentation improves reasoning](claims/argumentation-improves-reasoning.md) [~M] names prior knowledge as an open question on its claim page, not a tested moderator
rows.change: Lengthen preparation (a prior reading, or 20+ minutes with a structured source pack per side) and give an argument frame. Shorten open discussion. Defer SAC until a short explicit input on the evidence has been given.
rows.if: Expertise `novice` on the topic (cannot name evidence on either side)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Cut preparation and the source pack. Spend the time on the reversal and synthesis. Raise the synthesis bar: name the evidence that would settle the disagreement.
rows.if: Expertise `advanced` (graduate students, professionals who know the debate)

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page ("topics can be chosen to match learner maturity", "sentence stems"); [argumentation](claims/argumentation-improves-reasoning.md) [~M] reports larger effects in K-12 than higher education for online science argumentation, untested for SAC with children
rows.change: Use concrete, local questions (a class or school rule), pairs of two not four, sentence starters for restating ("You think… because…"), an oral synthesis recorded by the teacher, and shorter turns (about 2 minutes).
rows.if: Age `child` (upper primary)

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page (target learners); untested proposal for the adult change
rows.change: Use the default sequence. For adults, ask for the learner-valued goal explicitly, since adults often arrive with a held view; collect the starting position privately.
rows.if: Age `adolescent` or `adult` in civics, ethics, history or policy

rows.basis: [structured discussion methods](claims/structured-discussion-methods-improve-comprehension.md) [~M]: only a minority of discussion approaches improved comprehension or critical thinking (general discussion, not SAC)
rows.change: Put the content check in the source pack and in step 8 (an individual item on the evidence itself). Do not assume discussion delivered the content.
rows.if: Goal is `concept` or `principle` knowledge of the topic, not argument

rows.basis: untested proposal; perspective-taking and attitudes are not tested for SAC in this wiki
rows.change: Measure it separately, with a self-report or behaviour, at a `delayed` horizon. Do not infer it from a fair restatement in the session. Expect the effect of a single session to be small or short-lived.
rows.if: Goal is `attitude-motivation` (tolerance, openness to the other side)

rows.basis: untested proposal; [argumentation](claims/argumentation-improves-reasoning.md) [~M] includes online science argumentation, not SAC
rows.change: Use breakout rooms of four with a shared document whose columns are position / restatement / reversal / joint conclusion. Visit each room at the reversal. Give the timing in the document.
rows.if: Setting `online-instructor-led` (synchronous video)

rows.basis: untested proposal
rows.change: Run it asynchronously over `days-weeks`: positions posted, restatements as replies that the original author must accept, reversal posts, then a joint document. Grade the restatement and the individual position, not post counts. A shared misconception and a caricatured reversal will go unseen, so add a facilitator check before the synthesis.
rows.if: Setting `online-self-paced`, or no teacher present

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page ("strongest when the synthesis stage is treated as the instructional endpoint")
rows.change: Keep restate, reverse, synthesise and the individual check. Cut open discussion and do preparation from a one-page source sheet. Do not cut the synthesis or the individual check: they are what distinguish SAC from debate.
rows.if: `single-session` only (under 45 minutes)

rows.basis: [individual accountability](claims/cooperative-learning-group-rewards-and-individual-accountability.md) [~M], school studies of four weeks or more; untested for SAC
rows.change: Grade each learner's own position and restatement. If the joint report counts, make it a small share, or score it on each member's ability to defend a part chosen at random.
rows.if: High stakes: individual grades, or a joint report graded for the group

rows.basis: untested; from the earlier page ("emotional intensity", "performance pressure"); untested proposal for the language change
rows.change: Choose a question about a policy or interpretation, not a group of people. Let learners pick which position they prepare first. For learners working in a second language, give bilingual or simplified sources and allow written restatement.
rows.if: The topic is charged for someone present, or learners argue in a second language
