rows.basis: [Rater training](claims/peer-assessment-benefits-assessor.md) [+M] (moderator across 58 studies, roles pooled); [rubric guidance](claims/rubrics-improve-peer-feedback-quality.md) [+M] (MOOC writers; graduate students)
rows.change: Run collaborative evaluation on two anchors first; give three criteria with described levels and sentence frames; one draft per reviewer; the teacher reads and returns a sample of comments each cycle; keep the teacher's own comments on content accuracy.
rows.if: Reviewers are `novice` in the genre or domain

rows.basis: [Rubric guidance](claims/rubrics-improve-peer-feedback-quality.md) [~M]: in a graduate course a rubric changed comment content and restrained reflective and divergent commentary
rows.change: Let the author name the criteria and the questions to answer; drop frames and anchors; ask for one substantial alternative rather than a list of fixes; use the rubric as shared vocabulary, not a score sheet.
rows.if: Learners are `advanced` or practising professionals

rows.basis: [Collaborative writing](claims/collaborative-writing-improves-text-quality.md) [+S]: in one small randomised study, 10–11-year-olds writing in structured pairs gained more in their individual writing; that was co-writing, not peer review. [Peer assessment](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M] found no difference by education level
rows.change: Two criteria phrased as questions, with a picture or worked anchor; review in structured pairs, spoken first and then one written suggestion; the teacher models with a class draft each time; revise in the same or the next lesson.
rows.if: Learners are `child` (under 12)

rows.basis: [Peer accuracy](claims/peer-feedback-accuracy-depends-on-expertise.md) [~M]: AP English students' averaged rubric ratings correlated with expert scores about as well as teachers' did, in lower- as in higher-performing schools; correlational
rows.change: Anonymous drafts, four or five reviewers per essay with a well-specified rubric, and the average of their ratings shown to the author beside the comments; teacher reads flagged disagreements.
rows.if: Learners are `adolescent` secondary-school writers

rows.basis: Untested proposal. [Process writing](claims/process-writing-improves-writing-quality.md) [~M] did not improve struggling writers' compositions (grades 1–12), which is a reason not to rely on the cycle alone for them
rows.change: Short drafts or one section; a "what works and should stay" field first; spoken comments recorded or scribed; one criterion per cycle; the teacher adds one direct comment so the author is not relying on peers alone.
rows.if: Learners have low confidence or low literacy, or are struggling writers

rows.basis: [Peer accuracy](claims/peer-feedback-accuracy-depends-on-expertise.md) [~M]: secondary-school writing only; the correctness boundary is the claim pages' Discussion, untested
rows.change: Peers comment on clarity, structure and whether claims are supported; the teacher or an expert checks correctness; or give reviewers a check against a known answer.
rows.if: Quality turns on correctness (a calculation, code, a clinical or technical claim)

rows.basis: [Rubric guidance](claims/rubrics-improve-peer-feedback-quality.md) [+M]: MOOC writing raters, benefit concentrated on subjective, complex criteria and negligible on simple ones
rows.change: Spend calibration on those criteria; do not train or prompt for simple ones, which a checklist can cover.
rows.if: Criteria are subjective or complex (argument quality, audience fit), not simple and objective

rows.basis: [Assessor meta-analysis](claims/peer-assessment-benefits-assessor.md) [+M]: computer-mediated peer assessment did better than paper; [peer assessment](claims/peer-assessment-improves-performance.md) [+M] found no online/offline difference. The tool rules are untested
rows.change: Use a tool that assigns drafts at random, hides authors' names, locks a review once submitted and shows the author all reviews together; a calibration anchor before the first review; a deadline for the revision plan.
rows.if: `online-instructor-led` or `online-self-paced`, asynchronous

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: Run review asynchronously for everyone in one shared document or form, so no one reviews by ear; keep drafts short enough to read on a phone (one to two pages, or one section); in-room learners write comments in the same place rather than talking them across the table.
rows.if: Mixed modes: some learners in the room, some remote, or phone-only

rows.basis: [Peer feedback on writing](claims/peer-feedback-improves-writing.md) [+M]: number of peers did not moderate the effect; [peer accuracy](claims/peer-feedback-accuracy-depends-on-expertise.md) [~M]: averaged ratings, one subject, correlational
rows.change: Two to three reviewers per draft at random; the teacher reads comments only where an author flags a disagreement, and gives one class-wide note on the commonest problem; use averaged ratings rather than single reviews.
rows.if: One teacher for a large class, or no teacher reaches each pair

rows.basis: Untested proposal
rows.change: One short draft brought to the session; 10 minutes on one anchor; one review of one draft; 10 minutes to plan and start revising in the room; the author leaves with the plan.
rows.if: `single-session` only

rows.basis: [Rubric use](claims/rubrics-improve-student-work.md) [~M] came with more stress and a performance-avoidance orientation in pre-service teachers' self-assessment; carried to peer review
rows.change: Keep review formative; mark the final version (teacher) and, if anything, the quality of comments given against the teacher's reading; never the peer rating of a peer's work.
rows.if: High stakes: peer ratings would count towards marks

rows.basis: [Probing feedback with revise-and-resubmit](claims/probing-feedback-revise-resubmit-evidence.md) [+W]: a case study of teacher candidates in clinical placements, instructor feedback not peer; progress was not linear
rows.change: Review the real work product against the workplace's own standards; the author states what decision the draft must support; a senior colleague reviews alongside peers and requires a revise-and-resubmit where evidence is missing.
rows.if: Adults in a work setting (design teams, clinical or teaching placements)

rows.basis: [Authentic audiences](claims/authentic-audiences-improve-student-work.md) [+S]: seventh-graders' compositions to distant peers were rated higher than to the teacher; a small study, not of review
rows.change: Reviewers read as that audience: one criterion is "what would this reader do or misunderstand"; where possible include one reviewer from outside the class; the final version goes to the audience after revision, not the draft.
rows.if: The product will go to a real audience (a client, a publication, a public showing, a hiring panel)

rows.basis: [Anonymous sharing](claims/anonymity-mitigates-evaluation-apprehension.md) [~W], authors' account of one undergraduate physics course, no test
rows.change: Anonymous to authors (named to the teacher); "what works and should stay" first; random assignment of reviewers; no marks on reviews.
rows.if: Status or friendship differences, or reviews have hurt before

attitude-motivation.meaning: interest, beliefs, self-efficacy as the target

classroom.meaning: school or university class with a teacher

complex-skill.meaning: whole-task performance integrating several of the above

days-weeks.meaning: several sessions over up to about two months

novice.meaning: little or no prior knowledge of the target

online-instructor-led.meaning: digital with a live instructor or cohort

principle.meaning: rules, causal models, explanations to be understood to be applied

procedure.meaning: a step sequence to carry out
